They ignored him.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.7–8}}: {{lang|zh|"太祖到酸棗，諸軍兵十餘萬，日置酒高會，不圖進取。太祖責讓之，因為謀曰：「諸君聽吾計，使勃海引河內之衆臨孟津，酸棗諸將守成臯，據敖倉，塞轘轅、太谷，全制其險；使袁將軍率南陽之軍軍丹、析，入武關，以震三輔：皆高壘深壁，勿與戰，益為疑兵，示天下形勢，以順誅逆，可立定也。今兵以義動，持疑而不進，失天下之望，竊為諸君耻之！」邈等不能用。"}} ===Aftermath=== As Cao Cao had few troops left with him after the Battle of Xingyang, he travelled to [[Yang Province]] with [[Xiahou Dun]] to recruit soldiers. [[Chen Wen (Han dynasty)|Chen Wen]] ({{lang|zh|陳溫}}), the Inspector of Yang Province, and [[Zhou Xin (Han dynasty)|Zhou Xin]], the Administrator of Danyang Commandery ([[:zh:丹楊郡|丹楊郡]]), gave him over 4,000 troops. On the way back, when they passed by Longkang County ({{lang|zh|龍亢縣}}; in present-day [[Huaiyuan County]], Anhui), many soldiers started a mutiny and set fire to Cao Cao's tent at night, but he was able to escape.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"兵謀叛，夜燒太祖帳"}}. Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8 n. 1 (first n. 1)}} When Cao Cao reached Zhi ({{lang|zh|銍}}; west of present-day [[Suzhou, Anhui]]) and Jianping ({{lang|zh|建平}}; southwest of present-day [[Xiayi County]], Henan) counties later, he managed to regroup over 1,000 soldiers and lead them to a garrison in [[Henei Commandery]] (around present-day [[Wuzhi County]], Henan).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8}}: {{lang|zh|"太祖兵少，乃與夏侯惇等詣揚州募兵，刺史陳溫、丹楊太守周昕與兵四千餘人。還到龍亢，士卒多叛。至銍、建平，復收兵得千餘人，進屯河內。"}} Yuan Shao and [[Han Fu (warlord)|Han Fu]] thought of installing [[Liu Yu (warlord)|Liu Yu]], the Governor of [[Youzhou|You Province]], on the throne to replace Emperor Xian. When they sought Cao Cao's opinion,{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8}}: {{lang|zh|"袁紹與韓馥謀立幽州牧劉虞為帝，太祖拒之。"}} Cao Cao refused to support them and reaffirmed his allegiance to Emperor Xian.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"太祖答袁紹曰：「董卓之罪，暴於四海，吾等合大衆興義兵，遠近莫不響應，此以義動故也。今幼主微弱，制於姦臣，未有昌邑亡國之釁，而一旦改易，天下其孰安之？諸君北面，我自西向。」"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8 n. 1 (second n. 1)}} Yuan Shao's plan turned out to be unsuccessful because Liu Yu himself did not want to be emperor. Yuan Shao once invited Cao Cao to sit beside him and showed him a jade seal, indicating his imperial ambition, and a tacit request for Cao Cao's support. Finding this despicable, Cao Cao laughed at him.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8}}: {{lang|zh|"紹又嘗得一玉印，於太祖坐中舉向其肘，太祖由是笑而惡焉。"}} ==Military exploits in central China (191–199)== [[File:Cao Cao statue.jpg|thumb|left|198px|Statue of Cao Cao in [[Wuhan]]]] ===Pacifying Yan Province=== {{further|Heishan bandits}} Between 191 and 192, Yuan Shao appointed Cao Cao Administrator of [[Dong Commandery]]. This position allowed him to exact taxes and conscript soldiers. His first territorial command in that respect marks the beginning of his career as a warlord.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|pp=61–62}} During this time, he defeated the [[Heishan bandits]], who were causing trouble in the region, and some [[Xiongnu#Southern Xiongnu|Southern Xiongnu]] forces led by [[Yufuluo]] in [[Neihuang County]].{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.8–9}}: {{lang|zh|"黑山賊于毒、白繞、眭固等十餘萬衆略魏郡、東郡，王肱不能禦，太祖引兵入東郡，擊白繞于濮陽，破之。袁紹因表太祖為東郡太守，治東武陽。 ...太祖要擊眭固，又擊匈奴於夫羅於內黃，皆大破之。"}} Around the time, remnants from the Yellow Turban Rebellion swarmed into Yan Province from Qing Province. [[Liu Dai]], the Governor of Yan Province, was killed in a battle against the rebels. [[Bao Xin]], [[Chen Gong]] and others invited Cao Cao to replace Liu Dai as the Governor of Yan Province. Cao Cao defeated the rebels in battle and received the surrender of over 300,000 rebels and hundreds of thousands of civilians (the rebels' family members). From among them, he recruited the more battle-hardened ones to form a new military unit known as the Qingzhou Corps ({{lang|zh|青州兵}}).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.9–10}}: {{lang|zh|"青州黃巾衆百萬入兖州，...信乃與州吏萬潛等至東郡迎太祖領兖州牧。遂進兵擊黃巾于壽張東。 ...追黃巾至濟北。乞降。冬，受降卒三十餘萬，男女百餘萬口，收其精銳者，號為青州兵。"}} ===Conflict between Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu=== {{See also|Battle of Fengqiu}} [[Yuan Shu]] had disagreements with Yuan Shao so he contacted [[Gongsun Zan]], Yuan Shao's rival in northern China, for help in dealing with Yuan Shao. Gongsun Zan instructed [[Liu Bei]], Shan Jing ({{lang|zh|單經}}) and [[Tao Qian (Han dynasty)|Tao Qian]] to garrison at [[Gaotang County|Gaotang]], [[Pingyuan Commandery|Pingyuan]] and Fagan ({{lang|zh|發干}}; east of present-day [[Guan County, Shandong]]) counties respectively to put pressure on Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao allied with Cao Cao and defeated all the opposing forces. In the spring of 193, Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shu at the [[Battle of Fengqiu]] and returned to [[Dingtao County]] by summer.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.10}}: {{lang|zh|"袁術與紹有隙，術求援於公孫瓚，瓚使劉備屯高唐，單經屯平原，陶謙屯發干，以逼紹。太祖與紹會擊，皆破之。四年春，軍鄄城。荊州牧劉表斷術糧道，術引軍入陳留，屯封丘，黑山餘賊及於夫羅等佐之。術使將劉詳屯匡亭。太祖擊詳，術救之，與戰，大破之。術退保封丘，遂圍之，未合，術走襄邑，追到太壽，決渠水灌城。走寧陵，又追之，走九江。夏，太祖還軍定陶。"}} ===Conflict with Tao Qian=== {{main|Cao Cao's invasion of Xu Province}} {{further|Cao Song#Death }} Between 193 and 194, Cao Cao came into conflict with [[Tao Qian (Han dynasty)|Tao Qian]], the Governor of [[Xu Province]], and attacked Xu Province three times. The first attack took place in the autumn of 193, when Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian after the latter supported Que Xuan ([[:zh:闕宣|闕宣]]), who had committed treason by declaring himself emperor.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.10}}: {{lang|zh|"下邳闕宣聚衆數千人，自稱天子；徐州牧陶謙與共舉兵，取泰山華、費，略任城。秋，太祖征陶謙，下十餘城，謙守城不敢出。"}} The second and third invasions were triggered by the murder of Cao Cao's father, [[Cao Song]], in Xu Province, which occurred when Cao Song was en route to Qiao County ({{lang|zh|譙縣}}; present-day [[Bozhou]], Anhui) after his retirement. Although Tao Qian's culpability in the murder was questionable, Cao Cao nonetheless held him responsible for his father's death. During the invasions, Cao Cao conquered several territories in Xu Province and massacred thousands of civilians.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.11}}: {{lang|zh|"初，太祖父嵩去官後還譙...爲陶謙所害，故太祖志在復讎東伐。夏...復征陶謙，拔五城，遂略地至東海。還過郯，謙將曹豹與劉備屯郯東，要太祖。太祖擊破之，遂攻拔襄賁，所過多所殘戮。"}} Cao Cao's assault on Xu Province was so brutal that after one massacre the corpses of his victims stoppered up the nearby Si river ({{lang|zh|泗水}}).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|8}}.249}} His army tore down villages in its wake, ensuring refugees could not return, and ate all the chickens and dogs. Cao Cao only turned back when he received news that his base in Yan Province had fallen to [[Lü Bu]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} ===War with Lü Bu=== {{main|Battle of Yan Province|Battle of Xiapi}} In 194, Cao Cao's subordinates [[Zhang Miao (politician)|Zhang Miao]], [[Chen Gong]] and others rebelled against him in Yan Province and defected to the rival warlord [[Lü Bu]]. Many commanderies and counties in Yan Province responded to Lü Bu's call and defected to his side except for a few. Cao Cao aborted his campaign in [[Xu Province]] and returned to attack Lü Bu. In one battle at [[Puyang County]], he fell into an ambush and suffered some burns but managed to survive and escape. Cao Cao and Lü Bu were locked in a stalemate at Puyang County for over 100 days until Lü Bu left the county when his supplies ran out due to natural disasters such as locust plagues and droughts.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.11–12}}: {{lang|zh|"布出兵戰，先以騎犯青州兵。青州兵奔，太祖陳亂馳突火出，墜馬，燒左手掌。司馬樓異扶太祖上馬，遂引去。 ...與布相守百餘日。蝗蟲起，百姓大餓，布糧食亦盡，各引去。".}} Grain supplies were so limited that Cao Cao strongly considered an offer to serve under Yuan Shao, but was persuaded against it and ceased recruitment instead. He sent his army to collect food, but his numerically inferior forces were able to turn back an attack by Lü Bu that summer using deceptive tactics.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.12}}: {{lang|zh|"布復從東緍與陳宮將萬餘人來戰，時太祖兵少，設伏，縱奇兵擊，大破之。"}}{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"於是兵皆出取麥，在者不能千人，屯營不固。太祖乃令婦人守陴，悉兵拒之。屯西有大隄，其南樹木幽深。布疑有伏，...引軍屯南十餘里。明日復來，太祖隱兵隄裏，出半兵隄外。布益進，乃令輕兵挑戰，旣合，伏兵乃悉乘隄，步騎並進，大破之。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.12–13 n. 1 (second n. 1)}}. From 194 to late 195, Cao Cao attacked the territories in Yan Province and managed to retake them from Lü Bu. Lü Bu fled east to Xu Province and took refuge under [[Liu Bei]], who had succeeded [[Tao Qian (Han dynasty)|Tao Qian]] as the Governor of Xu Province earlier in 194. In the winter of 195, the central government officially designated Cao Cao as the Governor of Yan Province.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.11–12}}: {{lang|zh|"會張邈與陳宮叛迎呂布，郡縣皆應。 ...布夜走，太祖復攻，拔定陶，分兵平諸縣。布東奔劉備 ...冬十月，天子拜太祖兖州牧。"}} In 196, Lü Bu turned against his host and seized control of Xu Province from Liu Bei, but still allowed Liu Bei to remain in Xiaopei ({{lang|zh|小沛}}; present-day [[Pei County]], Jiangsu). Although he agreed to an alliance with [[Yuan Shu]] earlier, he broke his promise and severed ties with Yuan Shu when the latter declared himself emperor in early 197.{{harvnb|Zizhi Tongjian|1084|loc=volume {{strong|62}}}}: {{lang|zh|"[獻帝建安二年]...袁術稱帝於壽春，自稱仲家"}} Throughout 197, Lü Bu joined Cao Cao and others in a [[campaign against Yuan Shu]], who had become a public enemy because of his treasonous actions.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.15}}: {{lang|zh|"袁術欲稱帝於淮南，使人告呂布。布收其使，上其書。術怒，攻布，為布所破。"}} However, in 198, Lü Bu sided with Yuan Shu again and attacked Liu Bei, who lost and fled to join Cao Cao. In the winter of 198, Cao Cao and Liu Bei combined forces to attack Lü Bu and defeated him at the [[Battle of Xiapi]]. Lü Bu was captured and executed after his defeat. Cao Cao also pacified the eastern parts of Xu and [[Qing Province|Qing]] provinces along the coast.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.16}}: {{lang|zh|"呂布復為袁術使高順攻劉備，公遣夏侯惇救之，不利。備為順所敗。九月，公東征布。 ...月餘，布將宋憲、魏續等執陳宮，舉城降，生禽布、宮，皆殺之。太山臧霸、孫觀、吳敦、尹禮、昌豨各聚衆。布之破劉備也，霸等悉從布。布敗，獲霸等，公厚納待，遂割青、徐二州附於海以委焉，分琅邪、東海、北海為城陽、利城、昌慮郡。"}} ===Receiving Emperor Xian=== [[Emperor Xian of Han|Emperor Xian]] had been held hostage in [[Chang'an]] by [[Li Jue (Han dynasty)|Li Jue]], [[Guo Si]] and other former followers of Dong Zhuo. Around 195, when internal conflict broke out between Li Jue and Guo Si, Emperor Xian escaped from Chang'an and after a harrowing journey returned to the ruins of Luoyang, which Dong Zhuo had ordered to be destroyed by fire in 190 when moving the capital to Chang'an. In Luoyang, Emperor Xian came under the protection of [[Dong Cheng (Han dynasty)|Dong Cheng]], former bandit [[Yang Feng]], and other petty strongmen who have been characterised as "ragtag gangsters".{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|p=87}} The emperor sought refuge under Yuan Shao, but was rebuffed.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|pp=84–85}} In February or March 196, acting on the advice of [[Xun Yu]] and [[Cheng Yu]], Cao Cao sent [[Cao Hong]] west to fetch Emperor Xian but was blocked by Dong Cheng and Yuan Shu's subordinate Chang Nu ({{lang|zh|萇奴}}). Between March and April 196, Cao Cao defeated Yellow Turban remnants in Runan ([[:zh:汝南郡#漢代汝南郡|汝南]]) and Yingchuan ([[:zh:潁川郡|潁川]]) commanderies and was appointed General Who Establishes Virtue ({{lang|zh|建德將軍}}). In July or August 196, Cao Cao was promoted to General Who Garrisons the East ({{lang|zh|鎮東將軍}}) and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Fei Village ({{lang|zh|費亭侯}}) – the peerage previously held by his adoptive grandfather [[Cao Teng]].{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.13}}: {{lang|zh|"太祖將迎天子，諸將或疑，荀彧、程昱勸之，乃遣曹洪將兵西迎，衞將軍董承與袁術將萇奴拒險，洪不得進。汝南、潁川黃巾何儀、劉辟、黃邵、何曼等，衆各數萬，初應袁術，又附孫堅。二月，太祖進軍討破之，斬辟、邵等，儀及其衆皆降。天子拜太祖建德將軍，夏六月，遷鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。"}} Sometime between August and September 196, Cao Cao led his forces to the ruins of Luoyang and received Emperor Xian. The emperor granted Cao Cao a ceremonial axe and appointed him Manager of the Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat ([[:zh:錄尚書事|錄尚書事]]) and Colonel-Director of Retainers ([[:zh:司隷校尉|司隷校尉]]).''Xiandi Ji'': {{lang|zh|"又領司隷校尉。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.13 n. 2}}. As Luoyang was in bad shape, [[Dong Zhao (Three Kingdoms)|Dong Zhao]] and others advised Cao Cao to move the imperial capital to Xu ({{lang|zh|許}}; present-day [[Xuchang]], Henan). So, in October or early November 196, Cao Cao and his forces escorted Emperor Xian to Xuchang, which became the new imperial capital. Cao Cao had himself appointed General-in-Chief ([[:zh:大將軍 (東亞)#中國|大將軍]]) and promoted from a village marquis to a county marquis under the title "Marquis of Wuping" ({{lang|zh|武平侯}}), later characterised as ten thousand households.{{citation| author = Cao Cao| script-title=zh:十二月己亥令 | trans-title=Cao Cao's ''Apologia'' | date = 429 | orig-date=211 | script-work=zh:魏武故事 | work= Wei Wu gu shi | trans-work=The Memoirs of Lord Wu of Wei | quote=但食武平萬戶 }}
Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.32–34 n. 1}}. Since Dong Zhuo moved the capital from Luoyang to Chang'an in 190, the imperial court had been in a state of disorder. However, after Cao Cao received Emperor Xian and established the new imperial capital in Xuchang, order was restored,{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.13}}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，楊奉、韓暹以天子還洛陽，奉別屯梁。太祖遂至洛陽，衞京都，暹遁走。天子假太祖節鉞，錄尚書事。洛陽殘破，董昭等勸太祖都許。九月，車駕出轘轅而東，以太祖為大將軍，封武平侯。自天子西遷，朝廷日亂，至是宗廟社稷制度始立。"}} although Cao Cao did have the emperor's confidante Zhao Yan ([[:zh:趙彥 (東漢)|趙彥]]) killed for secretively keeping the emperor updated on the great affairs of state.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|p=116}} Cao Cao sent an imperial decree to [[Yuan Shao]] in Emperor Xian's name to appoint him as Grand Commandant ([[:zh:太尉#中國|太尉]]). Yuan Shao was unhappy because Grand Commandant ranked below Cao Cao's position, General-in-Chief, so he rejected the appointment. When Cao Cao heard about it, he gave up his position as General-in-Chief and offered it to Yuan Shao. Emperor Xian reappointed Cao Cao as [[Three Ducal Ministers|Minister of Works]] ({{lang|zh|司空}}) and acting General of Chariots and Cavalry ([[:zh:車騎將軍#東漢|車騎將軍]]). Struck by the difficulties Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu had faced in supplying their armies, as well as his own struggles with food supply in recent years, Cao Cao followed [[Zao Zhi]] and [[Han Hao]]'s suggestion to implement the ''[[tuntian]]'' system of agriculture{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.13}}: {{lang|zh|"於是以袁紹為太尉，紹恥班在公下，不肯受。公乃固辭，以大將軍讓紹。天子拜公司空，行車騎將軍。是歲用棗祗、韓浩等議，始興屯田。"}} to produce a sustainable supply of grain for his growing army.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"袁紹之在河北，軍人仰食桑椹。袁術在江、淮，取給蒲蠃。民人相食，州里蕭條。 ...是歲乃募民屯田許下，得穀百萬斛。於是州郡例置田官，所在積穀。征伐四方，無運糧之勞。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.14 n. 1}}. The ''tuntian'' agricultural colonies gave Cao Cao an advantage over his adversaries, allowing him to resettle internally displaced refugees, redevelop abandoned arable lands, shorten his supply lines, reduce the amount of defensive assets tasked to defend farms and granaries, and increase the area and productivity of lands held directly by the state.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|pp=91–92}} ===Battles with Zhang Xiu=== {{further|War between Cao Cao and Zhang Xiu}} In early 197, Cao Cao led his forces to Wancheng ({{lang|zh|宛城}}; present-day [[Wancheng District]] in [[Nanyang, Henan]]) to attack a rival warlord, [[Zhang Xiu (warlord)|Zhang Xiu]]. Zhang Xiu initially surrendered without a fight, but due to ill treatment changed his mind and attacked Cao Cao and caught him off guard. Cao Cao lost his eldest son [[Cao Ang]], nephew Cao Anmin ([[:zh:曹安民|曹安民]]) and close bodyguard [[Dian Wei]] in the battle. He returned to [[Xuchang]] after his defeat, but attacked Zhang Xiu again later that year and pacified Huyang ({{lang|zh|湖陽}}; southwest of present-day [[Tanghe County]], Henan) and Wuyin ({{lang|zh|舞陰}}; southeast of present-day [[Sheqi County]], Henan) counties. In early 198, he led another campaign against Zhang Xiu and besieged him in Rangcheng ({{lang|zh|穰城}}; present-day [[Dengzhou]], Henan) but withdrew his forces about two months later. Before retreating back to Xuchang, he set up an ambush and defeated Zhang Xiu's pursuing forces. In late 199, acting on [[Jia Xu]]'s advice, Zhang Xiu voluntarily surrendered to Cao Cao, who accepted his surrender.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.14–17}}: {{lang|zh|"二年春正月，公到宛。張繡降，旣而悔之，復反。公與戰，軍敗，為流矢所中，長子昂、弟子安民遇害。 ...冬十一月，公自南征，至宛。 ...湖陽降。攻舞陰，下之。 ...公將引還，繡兵來追，公軍不得進，連營稍前。 ...會明，賊謂公為遁也，悉軍來追。乃縱奇兵步騎夾攻，大破之。秋七月，公還許。 ...冬十一月，張繡率衆降，封列侯。"}} ===Campaign against Yuan Shu=== {{Further|Campaign against Yuan Shu}} In early 197, [[Yuan Shu]] declared himself emperor in Shouchun ({{lang|zh|壽春}}; present-day [[Shou County]], Anhui) – an act regarded as treason against [[Emperor Xian of Han|Emperor Xian]]. He soon came under attack by Cao Cao and various forces, including his former ally [[Lü Bu]]. In the autumn of 197, Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shu in battle, captured several of his officers, and had them executed. By 199, some months after Lü Bu's defeat at the [[Battle of Xiapi]], Yuan Shu, who was already in dire straits, wanted to abandon his lands in the [[Huainan]] region and head north to join Yuan Shao. Cao Cao sent [[Liu Bei]] and [[Zhu Ling (Three Kingdoms)|Zhu Ling]] to lead forces to intercept and block Yuan Shu in [[Xu Province]]. Yuan Shu died of illness while under siege by Liu Bei and Zhu Ling.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.15, 19}}: {{lang|zh|"秋九月，術侵陳，公東征之。術聞公自來，棄軍走，留其將橋蕤、李豐、梁綱、樂就；公到，擊破蕤等，皆斬之。術走渡淮。公還許。 ...袁術自敗於陳，稍困，袁譚自青州遣迎之。術欲從下邳北過，公遣劉備、朱靈要之。會術病死。"}} ==War with Yuan Shao (199–202)== [[File:Cao Cao's conquest of northern China 200–207.png|400px|thumb|Cao Cao's conquests from the Yuan clan 200–207]] {{main|Battle of Guandu}} ===Background=== While Cao Cao was waging wars throughout central China in the 190s, Yuan Shao defeated his rival [[Gongsun Zan]] at the [[Battle of Yijing]] in 199, after which he controlled four provinces in northern China ([[Ji Province|Ji]], [[Bing Province|Bing]], [[Qing Province|Qing]] and [[Youzhou|You]]) and gained command of thousands of troops. A power struggle between Cao Cao and Yuan Shao became inevitable by early 199. In the autumn of 199, Cao Cao dispatched troops to Liyang County ({{lang|zh|黎陽縣}}; present-day [[Xun County]], Henan) and sent [[Zang Ba]] and others to capture some territories in Qing Province while leaving [[Yu Jin]] to guard the southern bank of the [[Yellow River]]. In winter, he mobilised his forces and deployed them at Guandu ({{lang|zh|官渡}}; present-day Guandu Town, [[Zhongmu County]], Henan).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.17}}: {{lang|zh|"是時袁紹旣并公孫瓚，兼四州之地，衆十餘萬，將進軍攻許... 秋八月，公進軍黎陽，使臧霸等入青州破齊、北海、東安，留于禁屯河上。九月，公還許，分兵守官渡。 ...十二月，公軍官渡。"}} ====Campaign against Liu Bei in Xu Province==== Around this time, [[Cheng Yu]] and Guo Jia had warned Cao Cao against allowing Liu Bei to leave [[Xuchang]] but it was too late because Cao Cao had already sent Liu Bei to intercept and block Yuan Shu. Earlier, when he was still in Xuchang, Liu Bei had secretly joined a plot initiated by [[Dong Cheng (Han dynasty)|Dong Cheng]] and others to get rid of Cao Cao. After leaving Xuchang, Liu Bei headed to Xu Province, killed the provincial inspector Che Zhou ([[:zh:車冑|車冑]]), and seized control of Xu Province. Cao Cao sent Liu Dai ({{lang|zh|劉岱}}){{efn|This Liu Dai ({{lang|zh|劉岱}}) was not the same person as [[Liu Dai]]; courtesy name Gongshan), the Governor of Yan Province, who was killed in 192.}} and [[Wang Zhong (Three Kingdoms)|Wang Zhong]] to attack Liu Bei but they were defeated.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.18}}: {{lang|zh|"程昱、郭嘉聞公遣備，言於公曰：「劉備不可縱。」公悔，追之不及。備之未東也，陰與董承等謀反，至下邳，遂殺徐州刺史車冑，舉兵屯沛。遣劉岱、王忠擊之，不克。"}} In February 200, Cao Cao got wind of Dong Cheng's plot and had all the conspirators arrested and executed. He then led a campaign to retake Xu Province from Liu Bei, defeated him, and captured his family. Liu Bei's general [[Guan Yu]], who was guarding Xu Province's capital, Xiapi ({{lang|zh|下邳}}; present-day [[Pizhou]], Jiangsu), surrendered and temporarily served Cao Cao. Liu Bei fled north to join Yuan Shao after his defeat. Some of Cao Cao's subordinates initially expressed worries that Yuan Shao might attack them while Cao Cao was away in Xu Province, but, as Cao Cao accurately predicted,{{efn|See [[Guo Jia#Suggestion to Cao Cao to attack Liu Bei first before attacking Yuan Shao]]. This account says that Guo Jia was the one who predicted that [[Yuan Shao]] would not make any move while Cao Cao was attacking [[Liu Bei]].}} Yuan Shao did not make any advances throughout this period of time,{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.18}}: {{lang|zh|"五年春正月，董承等謀泄，皆伏誅。公將自東征備，諸將皆曰：「與公爭天下者，袁紹也。今紹方來而棄之東，紹乘人後，若何？」公曰：「夫劉備，人傑也，今不擊，必為後患。袁紹雖有大志，而見事遟，必不動也。」郭嘉亦勸公，遂東擊備，破之... 公還官渡，紹卒不出。"}} possibly due to Cao Cao's general [[Yu Jin]]'s raiding in the south of Yuan Shao's territory.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|17}}.523}} ===Early stages=== {{main|Battle of Boma|Battle of Yan Ford}} From early to mid 200, the forces of Cao Cao and Yuan Shao clashed in two separate engagements at Boma ({{lang|zh|白馬}}; present-day [[Hua County]], Henan) and Yan Ford ({{lang|zh|延津}}; near present-day [[Yanjin County, Henan|Yanjin County]], Henan). At Boma, Yuan Shao sent [[Guo Tu]], [[Chunyu Qiong]] and [[Yan Liang]] to besiege Cao Cao's general Liu Yan ({{lang|zh|劉延}}), but the siege was lifted after about two months when Cao Cao personally led an army to relief Liu Yan. Guan Yu slew Yan Liang in the midst of battle. While Cao Cao and his troops were evacuating Boma's residents, Yuan Shao's forces led by [[Wen Chou]] and Liu Bei caught up with them at Yan Ford, but were defeated and Wen Chou was killed in battle. Cao Cao returned to his main camp at Guandu while Yuan Shao moved to Yangwu County ({{lang|zh|陽武縣}}; southwest of present-day [[Yuanyang County, Henan]]). Around this time, Guan Yu left Cao Cao and returned to Liu Bei.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.19 }}: {{lang|zh|"二月，紹遣郭圖、淳于瓊、顏良攻東郡太守劉延於白馬，紹引兵至黎陽，將渡河。夏四月，公北救延。 ...公乃引軍兼行趣白馬，未至十餘里，良大驚，來逆戰。使張遼、關羽前登，擊破，斬良。遂解白馬圍，徙其民，循河而西。紹於是渡河追公軍，至延津南。 ...時騎不滿六百，遂縱兵擊，大破之，斬醜、良。醜、良皆紹名將也，再戰，悉禽，紹軍大震。公還軍官渡。紹進保陽武。關羽亡歸劉備。"}} {{see also|Guan Yu#Leaving Cao Cao}} ===Stalemate at Guandu and the raid on Wuchao=== In late 200, Yuan Shao led his forces to attack Cao Cao at Guandu. Both sides were locked in a stalemate for months and Cao Cao's supplies were gradually running out and his men were growing weary. During this time, Yuan Shao sent Liu Bei to contact a rebel chief, Liu Pi ([[:zh:劉辟 (東漢)|劉辟]]), in [[Runan Commandery]] (near present-day [[Xinyang]], Henan) and join Liu Pi in making a sneak attack on Cao Cao's base in Xuchang while Cao Cao was away at Guandu. However, Liu Bei and Liu Pi were defeated and driven back by Cao Cao's general [[Cao Ren]]. During this time, [[Sun Ce]], a warlord based in the [[Jiangnan|Jiangdong]] region, also contemplated attacking Xuchang and taking Emperor Xian hostage. However, he was assassinated before he could execute his plan.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.20–21 }}: {{lang|zh|"孫策聞公與紹相持，乃謀襲許，未發，為刺客所殺。汝南降賊劉辟等叛應紹，略許下。紹使劉備助辟，公使曹仁擊破之。備走，遂破辟屯。袁紹運穀車數千乘至，公用荀攸計，遣徐晃、史渙邀擊，大破之，盡燒其車。公與紹相拒連月，雖比戰斬將，然衆少糧盡，士卒疲乏。"}} In the winter of 200, following the advice of [[Xu You (Han dynasty)|Xu You]], a defector from Yuan Shao's side, Cao Cao left [[Cao Hong]] behind to defend his main camp at Guandu while he personally led 5,000 riders to raid Yuan Shao's supply depot at Wuchao ({{lang|zh|烏巢}}; southeast of present-day [[Yanjin County, Henan]]), which was guarded by [[Chunyu Qiong]]. Cao Cao succeeded in destroying Yuan Shao's supplies. When Yuan Shao heard that Wuchao was under attack, he sent [[Zhang He]] and [[Zhang He#Defection to Cao Cao|Gao Lan]] to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao Cao's attention away from Wuchao. However, Zhang He and Gao Lan, already frustrated with Yuan Shao, destroyed their own camps and led their troops to defect to Cao Cao's side. The morale of Yuan Shao's army fell drastically and they were utterly defeated by Cao Cao's forces, after which Yuan Shao hastily crossed the [[Yellow River]] and retreated back to northern China. Much of his supplies and many of his soldiers were captured by Cao Cao. Cao Cao also obtained several letters written by spies from his side to Yuan Shao, but he refused to conduct an investigation to find out who the spies were, and instead ordered all the letters to be burnt. Many commanderies in [[Ji Province]] surrendered to Cao Cao.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.21}}: {{lang|zh|"公謂運者曰：「却十五日為汝破紹，不復勞汝矣。」冬十月，紹遣車運穀，使淳于瓊等五人將兵萬餘人送之，宿紹營北四十里。紹謀臣許攸貪財，紹不能足，來奔，因說公擊瓊等。左右疑之，荀攸、賈詡勸公。公乃留曹洪守，自將步騎五千人夜往，會明至。瓊等望見公兵少，出陳門外。公急擊之，瓊退保營，遂攻之。紹遣騎救瓊。左右或言「賊騎稍近，請分兵拒之」。公怒曰：「賊在背後，乃白！」士卒皆殊死戰，大破瓊等，皆斬之。紹初聞公之擊瓊，謂長子譚曰：「就彼攻瓊等，吾攻拔其營，彼固無所歸矣！」乃使張郃、高覽攻曹洪。郃等聞瓊破，遂來降。紹衆大潰，紹及譚棄軍走，渡河。追之不及，盡收其輜重圖書珍寶，虜其衆。公收紹書中，得許下及軍中人書，皆焚之。冀州諸郡多舉城邑降者。"}} ===Aftermath=== In the summer of 201, Cao Cao led his forces across the Yellow River and attacked Yuan Shao again, inflicting another crushing defeat on him at the [[Battle of Cangting]] and pacifying the territories in the area. In autumn, Cao Cao returned to Xuchang and sent Cai Yang ([[:zh:蔡揚|蔡揚]]) to attack Liu Bei, who had left Yuan Shao and allied with another rebel chief, Gong Du ([[:zh:龔都|共都]]),{{efn|Gong Du's name is spelt {{lang|zh|共都}} in Cao Cao's biography, and {{lang|zh|龔都}} in Liu Bei's.}} in Runan Commandery. Liu Bei defeated and killed Cai Yang in battle.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|32}}.876}}: {{lang|zh|"紹遣先主將本兵復至汝南，與賊龔都等合，眾數千人。曹公遣蔡陽擊之，為先主所殺。"}} Cao Cao personally led his forces to attack Liu Bei, who fled south upon learning Cao Cao himself was in command. He took shelter under governor [[Liu Biao]] in [[Jing Province]].{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.22}}: {{lang|zh|"六年夏四月，揚兵河上，擊紹倉亭軍，破之。紹歸，復收散卒，攻定諸叛郡縣。九月，公還許。紹之未破也，使劉備略汝南，汝南賊共都等應之。遣蔡揚擊都，不利，為都所破。公南征備。備聞公自行，走奔劉表，都等皆散。"}} The following spring, while in his hometown, Cao Cao issued a proclamation characterising his military actions as a righteous uprising.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.22–23}}: {{lang|zh|"七年春正月，公軍譙，令曰：「吾起義兵，爲天下除暴亂。舊土人民，死喪略盡，國中終日行，不見所識，使吾悽愴傷懷。其舉義兵已來，將士絕無後者，求其親戚以後之，授上田，官給耕牛，置學師以教之。爲存者立廟，使祀其先人，魂而有靈，吾百年之後何恨哉！」"}} ==Unification of northern China (202–207)== ===Battle of Liyang=== {{main|Battle of Liyang}} Yuan Shao died of illness in the early summer of 202 and was succeeded by his third son, [[Yuan Shang]]. In autumn, Cao Cao attacked Yuan Shang and his eldest brother [[Yuan Tan]] and defeated them, forcing them to retreat and hold up inside their fortresses. In the spring of 203, Cao Cao attacked the Yuan brothers again and defeated them. In summer, he advanced towards [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei) and returned to [[Xuchang]] later, leaving behind Jia Xin ([[:zh:賈信|賈信]]) to defend Liyang County ({{lang|zh|黎陽縣}}; present-day [[Xun County]], Henan).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.23 }}: {{lang|zh|"紹自軍破後，發病歐血，夏五月死。小子尚代，譚自號車騎將軍，屯黎陽。秋九月，公征之，連戰。譚、尚數敗退，固守。 八年春三月，攻其郭，乃出戰，擊，大破之，譚、尚夜遁。夏四月，進軍鄴。五月還許，留賈信屯黎陽。"}} Afterwards, Cao Cao issued an order establishing schools in each of his counties with 500 or more households.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.24 }}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，令曰：「...其令郡國各修文學，縣滿五百戶置校官，選其鄉之俊造而教學之...」"}} ===Defeating Yuan Shao's heirs=== {{main|Battle of Ye|Battle of Nanpi}} Some months after Cao Cao left northern China and returned to the south, internal conflict broke out between [[Yuan Shang]] and [[Yuan Tan]] as the brothers started fighting over Ji Province. Yuan Tan, who lost to Yuan Shang, surrendered to Cao Cao and sought his help in dealing with his third brother. Cao Cao agreed to assist Yuan Tan, so, in the winter of 203, he returned to northern China. Between spring and autumn in 204, Cao Cao attacked Yuan Shang in his base at [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] and conquered the city. Yuan Shang fled further north to [[Zhongshan Commandery]] ([[:zh:中山郡#東漢|中山郡]]; around present-day [[Dingzhou]], Hebei). After capturing Ye, Cao Cao visited Yuan Shao's tomb, weeping for his childhood friend-turned-rival, and spared no effort assuaging Yuan Shao's widow. To the delight of the people in Hebei, Cao Cao issued an order exempting them from paying taxes for that year and clamped down on the power of influential landlords in the area. When [[Emperor Xian of Han|Emperor Xian]] offered to appoint Cao Cao as the Governor of Ji Province, Cao Cao declined, preferring to stick to his appointment as the Governor of Yan Province.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.24–26}}: {{lang|zh|"八月，公征劉表，軍西平。公之去鄴而南也，譚、尚爭冀州，譚為尚所敗，走保平原。尚攻之急，譚遣辛毗乞降請救。諸將皆疑，荀攸勸公許之，公乃引軍還。冬十月，到黎陽，為子整與譚結婚。 ...九年春正月，濟河，遏淇水入白溝以通糧道。二月，尚復攻譚，留蘇由、審配守鄴。 ...八月，審配兄子榮夜開所守城東門內兵。配逆戰，敗，生禽配，斬之，鄴定。公臨祀紹墓，哭之流涕；慰勞紹妻，還其家人寶物，賜雜繒絮，廩食之。 ...九月，令曰：「河北罹袁氏之難，其令無出今年租賦！」重豪彊兼幷之法，百姓喜恱。天子以公領冀州牧，公讓還兖州。"}} While Cao Cao was attacking Yuan Shang in Ye, Yuan Tan, who had previously allied with Cao Cao against his third brother, took over some of Yuan Shang's territories and troops for himself. Cao Cao wrote to Yuan Tan to reprimand him for not adhering to their earlier agreement. Yuan Tan became afraid so he retreated to [[Nanpi County]]. In the spring of 205, Cao Cao attacked Yuan Tan, defeated him, and executed him along with his family. Ji Province was completely pacified. Around the same time, Yuan Shang had fled to join his second brother [[Yuan Xi]] but Yuan Xi was betrayed by his subordinates Jiao Chu ([[:zh:焦觸|焦觸]]) and Zhang Nan ([[:zh:張南 (東漢)|張南]]), who surrendered to Cao Cao. The Yuan brothers had no choice but to head further north to take shelter under the [[Wuhuan]] tribes.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.26–27 }}: {{lang|zh|"公之圍鄴也，譚略取甘陵、安平、勃海、河閒。尚敗，還中山。譚攻之，尚奔故安，遂幷其衆。公遺譚書，責以負約，與之絕婚，女還，然後進軍。譚懼，拔平原，走保南皮。十二月，公入平原，略定諸縣。十年春正月，攻譚，破之，斬譚，誅其妻子，冀州平。 ...是月，袁熙大將焦觸、張南等叛攻熙、尚，熙、尚奔三郡烏丸。觸等舉其縣降，封為列侯。"}} In the spring of 206, Cao Cao attacked Yuan Shao's maternal nephew [[Gao Gan]], who had surrendered to him initially but rebelled later, and defeated Gao Gan at Hu Pass ({{lang|zh|壺關}}; in present-day [[Huguan County]], Shanxi). In autumn, Cao Cao started a campaign against the pirates led by Guan Cheng ({{nowrap|{{lang|zh|管承}}}}). He sent [[Yue Jin]] and [[Li Dian]] to attack Guan Cheng and pacified the eastern coast.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.28 }}: {{lang|zh|"初，袁紹以甥高幹領幷州牧，公之拔鄴，幹降，遂以為刺史。幹聞公討烏丸，乃以州叛，執上黨太守，舉兵守壺關口。遣樂進、李典擊之，幹還守壺關城。十一年春正月，公征幹。幹聞之，乃留其別將守城，走入匈奴，求救於單于，單于不受。公圍壺關三月，拔之。幹遂走荊州，上洛都尉王琰捕斬之。秋八月，公東征海賊管承，至淳于，遣樂進、李典擊破之，承走入海島。割東海之襄賁、郯、戚以益瑯邪，省昌慮郡。"}} ===Campaign against the Wuhuan=== {{main|Battle of White Wolf Mountain}} In the summer of 206, Cao Cao received the surrender of thousands of [[Heishan bandits]] led by [[Zhang Yan (Han dynasty)|Zhang Yan]]. Around the time, Zhao Du ({{lang|zh|趙犢}}) and Huo Nu ({{lang|zh|霍奴}}) killed the Inspector of [[Youzhou|You Province]] and the Administrator of Zhuo Commandery ({{lang|zh|涿郡}}; around present-day [[Zhuozhou]], Hebei), while the Wuhuan tribes from three commanderies attacked Xianyu Fu ([[:zh:鮮于輔|鮮于輔]]) at Guangping County ({{lang|zh|獷平縣}}; west of present-day [[Miyun District]] in Beijing). In early autumn, Cao Cao personally led a campaign against them and defeated Zhao Du and Huo Nu, after which his army crossed the Lu River ({{lang|zh|潞河}}; in present-day [[Tongzhou District, Beijing|Tongzhou District]], Beijing) to help Xianyu Fu by attacking the Wuhuan. They succeeded in driving the Wuhuan away. Cao Cao returned to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] by winter.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.27 }}: {{lang|zh|"夏四月，黑山賊張燕率其衆十餘萬降，封為列侯。故安趙犢、霍奴等殺幽州刺史、涿郡太守。三郡烏丸攻鮮于輔於獷平。秋八月，公征之，斬犢等，乃渡潞河救獷平，烏丸奔走出塞。 ...冬十月，公還鄴。"}} Throughout the period of civil wars during the late Eastern Han dynasty, the Wuhuan tribes in northern China had been taking advantage of the situation to invade You Province, capture and enslave thousands of people living in the area. When Yuan Shao had been in power in northern China, he maintained friendly ties with the Wuhuan, so [[Yuan Shang]] and [[Yuan Xi]] found refuge under the Wuhuan chieftains. In 207, Cao Cao led a campaign against the Wuhuan and the Yuan brothers and scored a decisive victory over them at the [[Battle of White Wolf Mountain]] later that year. The campaign was difficult and dangerous, and Cao Cao rewarded his counselors who had advised him against undertaking it.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|p=236}} Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi fled further northeast to [[Liaodong]] to take shelter under the warlord [[Gongsun Kang]]. When Cao Cao's generals were preparing for an invasion of Liaodong, Cao Cao stopped them and predicted that Gongsun Kang would kill the Yuan brothers. Cao Cao was right, as Gongsun Kang arrested and executed the Yuan brothers because he sensed that they posed a threat to him. He then sent their heads to Cao Cao as a gesture of goodwill. Northern China was basically pacified and unified under Cao Cao's control by then.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.28 }}: {{lang|zh|"三郡烏丸承天下亂，破幽州，略有漢民合十餘萬戶。袁紹皆立其酋豪為單于，以家人子為己女，妻焉。遼西單于蹋頓尤彊，為紹所厚，故尚兄弟歸之，數入塞為害。公將征之，鑿渠，自呼沲入泒水，名平虜渠；又從泃河口鑿入潞河，名泉州渠，以通海。"}}{{pb}}{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.29–30 }}: {{lang|zh|"將北征三郡烏丸， ...八月，登白狼山，卒與虜遇，衆甚盛。公車重在後，被甲者少，左右皆懼。公登高，望虜陳不整，乃縱兵擊之，使張遼為先鋒，虜衆大崩，斬蹋頓及名王已下，胡、漢降者二十餘萬口。遼東單于速僕丸及遼西、北平諸豪，棄其種人，與尚、熙奔遼東，衆尚有數千騎。初，遼東太守公孫康恃遠不服。及公破烏丸，或說公遂征之，尚兄弟可禽也。公曰：「吾方使康斬送尚、熙首，不煩兵矣。」九月，公引兵自柳城還，康即斬尚、熙及速僕丸等，傳其首。諸將或問：「公還而康斬送尚、熙，何也？」公曰：「彼素畏尚等，吾急之則幷力，緩之則自相圖，其勢然也。」十一月至易水，代郡烏丸行單于普富盧、上郡烏丸行單于那樓將其名王來賀。"}} In the spring of 207, Cao Cao announced he would be distributing his wealth amongst those who had aided him, and enfeoffed over twenty of his followers as marquises, with lesser emoluments for the remainder.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.28}}: {{lang|zh|"於是大封功臣二十餘人，皆爲列侯，其餘各以次受封。"}} ==Red Cliffs campaign (207–211)== [[File:新刊校正古本大字音释三国志通俗演义 明万历十九年书林周曰校刊本 096.jpg|thumb|Ming dynasty woodblock print of [[Romance of the Three Kingdoms]] depicting Cao Cao, attended by his adjutants and soldiers, meeting with [[Pang Tong]].]] ===Background=== Cao Cao returned to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei) in the spring of 208 after pacifying northern China. He ordered the construction of Xuanwu Pool ({{lang|zh|玄武池}}) to train his troops in naval warfare. He also implemented changes to the political system by abolishing the [[Three Ducal Ministers]] and replacing them with the offices of the [[Chancellor (China)|Imperial Chancellor]] ({{lang|zh|丞相}}) and Imperial Counsellor ([[:zh:御史大夫|御史大夫]]).{{efn|The [[Three Ducal Ministers]] were the three highest ranked officials in the [[government of the Han dynasty]] and they collectively served as the heads of government. When Cao Cao abolished these three posts and replaced them with the office of the [[Chancellor (China)|Imperial Chancellor]] (which he assumed shortly after), he was consolidating power so that he would become the sole head of government without having to share power with any other person.}} He was officially appointed as Imperial Chancellor in July 208.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.30 }}: {{lang|zh|"十三年春正月，公還鄴，作玄武池以肄舟師。漢罷三公官，置丞相、御史大夫。夏六月，以公為丞相。"}} Around this time he had the famous scholar [[Kong Rong]] – later listed by Cao Cao's own son Cao Pi as one of the foremost literary talents of the age{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|p=420}} – put to death for insouciance, along with his family.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|pp=116–117}} In August 208, Cao Cao launched a southern campaign to attack [[Liu Biao]], the governor of [[Jing Province]]. Liu Biao died of illness in the following month and was succeeded by his younger son, [[Liu Cong (Han dynasty)|Liu Cong]]. Liu Cong was stationed at [[Xiangyang]] while Liu Bei moved from [[Xinye County]] to Fancheng ({{lang|zh|樊城}}; present-day [[Fancheng District]] in Xiangyang, Hubei). Liu Cong surrendered in late September or October 208 when Cao Cao and his forces reached Xinye County. Liu Bei and his followers fled towards Xiakou ({{lang|zh|夏口}}; in present-day [[Wuhan]]) to join Liu Biao's elder son, [[Liu Qi (Liu Biao's son)|Liu Qi]]. Cao Cao sent 5,000 riders to pursue Liu Bei and after covering {{cvt|150|km|miles}} in twenty-four hours{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010| p=331 n. 86 }} they caught up with him and defeated him at the [[Battle of Changban]]. Liu Bei managed to escape and retreat safely to Xiakou with a few followers, but lost most of his supplies and equipment to the enemy.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|32}}.878 }}: {{lang|zh|"曹公以江陵有軍實，恐先主據之，乃釋輜重，輕軍到襄陽。聞先主已過，曹公將精騎五千急追之，一日一夜行三百餘里，及於當陽之長坂。先主棄妻子，與諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等數十騎走，曹公大獲其人衆輜重。"}} Liu Bei later formed an alliance with the warlord [[Sun Quan]], who controlled the territories in the [[Wu (region)|Wuyue region]] in southern China. Meanwhile, Cao Cao advanced towards [[Jiangling County]] and reformed Jing Province's administration. He also rewarded those who helped him gain Jing Province, including those from Liu Cong's side who persuaded Liu Cong to surrender to him. Cao Cao appointed [[Wen Ping]], a former general under Liu Biao, as the Administrator of [[Jiangxia Commandery]] (around present-day [[Xinzhou District, Wuhan]], Hubei) and put him in command of some of his troops. He also recruited members of the [[Landed gentry in China|scholar-gentry]] in Jing Province, such as [[Han Song (Han dynasty)|Han Song]] ([[:zh:韓嵩|韓嵩]]) and [[Deng Yi (government official)|Deng Yi]], to serve under him.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.30 }}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，公南征劉表。八月，表卒，其子琮代，屯襄陽，劉備屯樊。九月，公到新野，琮遂降，備走夏口。公進軍江陵，下令荊州吏民，與之更始。乃論荊州服從之功，侯者十五人，以劉表大將文聘為江夏太守，使統本兵，引用荊州名士韓嵩、鄧義等。"}} ===Battle of Red Cliffs=== [[File:Battle of Red Cliffs 208 extended map-en.svg|thumb|400px|[[Battle of Red Cliffs|Red Cliffs campaign]] map, showing Cao Cao's pursuit of Liu Bei, [[Battle of Changban|Changban]], [[Battle of Red Cliffs|Red Cliffs]], Cao Cao's retreat and [[Battle of Jiangling (208)|Jiangling]]]] {{main|Battle of Red Cliffs}} [[Liu Zhang (warlord)|Liu Zhang]], the Governor of [[Yi Province]] (present-day [[Sichuan]] and [[Chongqing]]), had received orders to help Cao Cao recruit soldiers from his province, so he sent the new conscripts to [[Jiangling County]]. In late December 208 or January 209, [[Sun Quan]] helped Liu Bei by [[Battle of Hefei (208)|attacking Cao Cao's garrison at Hefei]]. Around the same time, Cao Cao led his forces from Jiangling County to attack Liu Bei. When they reached Baqiu ({{lang|zh|巴丘}}; present-day [[Yueyang]], Hunan), Cao Cao ordered Zhang Xi ({{lang|zh|張憙}}) to lead a separate army to reinforce Hefei, and Sun Quan withdrew his forces from Hefei upon receiving news of Zhang Xi's arrival.{{efn|[[Sun Sheng (Jin dynasty)|Sun Sheng]] commented in his ''Yitong Ping'' ({{lang|zh|異同評}}) that the ''Wu Zhi'' ({{lang|zh|吳志}}) claimed that the [[Battle of Hefei (208)]] took place after the Battle of Red Cliffs. This was contrary to what was mentioned in Cao Cao's biography (that Hefei came before Red Cliffs). Sun Sheng considered the ''Wu Zhi'' account to be the correct one.[[Sun Sheng (Jin dynasty)|Sun Sheng]], ''Yitong ping'': {{lang|zh|"案吳志，劉備先破公軍，然後權攻合肥，而此記云權先攻合肥，後有赤壁之事。二者不同，吳志為是。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.31–32 n. 2}}.}} Cao Cao's forces advanced to Red Cliffs ({{lang|zh|赤壁}}) and engaged the allied forces of Liu Bei and Sun Quan, but lost the battle. Around that time, an epidemic disease had broken out in Cao Cao's army and many had died, so Cao Cao ordered a retreat. Liu Bei then went on to conquer the four [[Commandery (China)|commanderies]] in southern Jing Province.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.30–31}}: {{lang|zh|"益州牧劉璋始受徵役，遣兵給軍。十二月，孫權為備攻合肥。公自江陵征備，至巴丘，遣張憙救合肥。權聞憙至，乃走。公至赤壁，與備戰，不利。於是大疫，吏士多死者，乃引軍還。備遂有荊州、江南諸郡。"}} After his defeat at Red Cliffs, Cao Cao led his remaining forces through Huarong Trail ({{lang|zh|華容道}}; near present-day [[Jianli County]], Hubei) as they were retreating. The area was very muddy and inaccessible and there were strong winds. Cao Cao ordered his weaker soldiers to carry straw and hay to lay out the path ahead so that his horsemen could proceed. The weaker soldiers ended up being stuck in the mud and many were trampled to death by the riders. Cao Cao expressed joy after he and his surviving men managed to get out of Huarong Trail safely, albeit suffering much losses. His generals were puzzled so they asked him why. Cao Cao remarked: "Liu Bei, my friend, doesn't think fast enough. If he had set fire earlier, we wouldn't have been able to get out alive." Liu Bei did think of setting fire but it was too late as Cao Cao had already escaped.Yue Zi, ''Shanyang Gong zaiji'': {{lang|zh|"公船艦為備所燒，引軍從華容道步歸，遇泥濘，道不通，天又大風，悉使羸兵負草填之，騎乃得過。羸兵為人馬所蹈藉，陷泥中，死者甚衆。軍旣得出，公大喜，諸將問之，公曰：「劉備，吾儔也。但得計少晚；向使早放火，吾徒無類矣。」備尋亦放火而無所及。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.31 n. 2 }}. ===After the Red Cliffs campaign=== In the spring of 209, Cao Cao reached Qiao County ({{lang|zh|譙縣}}; present-day [[Bozhou]], Anhui), where he ordered small boats to be built and staged a naval drill. In autumn, he sailed along the [[Huai River]] to the garrison at [[Hefei]], where he issued an order for local officials to provide relief to the families of soldiers who had died in battle. He then established an administration in [[Yang Province]] and started a ''[[tuntian]]'' system in Quebei ({{lang|zh|芍陂}}; south of present-day [[Shou County]], Anhui). He returned to Qiao County in winter.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.32}}: {{lang|zh|"十四年春三月，軍至譙，作輕舟，治水軍。秋七月，自渦入淮，出肥水，軍合肥。辛未，令曰：「自頃已來，軍數征行，或遇疫氣，吏士死亡不歸，家室怨曠，百姓流離，而仁者豈樂之哉？不得已也。其令死者家無基業不能自存者，縣官勿絕廩，長吏存恤撫循，以稱吾意。」置揚州郡縣長吏，開芍陂屯田。十二月，軍還譙。"}} In the winter of 210, Cao Cao had a [[Bronze Sparrow Pavilion|Bronze Sparrow Platform]] constructed in [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]].{{efn|The name of the Bronze Sparrow Platform was written as {{zh|labels=no|c=銅爵臺|p=tóng jué tái}} instead of {{zh|labels=no|c=銅雀臺|p= tóng què tái}}. The former has been superseded by the latter, which has become the more common term used in modern times to refer to the platform. See the [https://www.zdic.net/hant/%E9%8A%85%E9%9B%80%E8%87%BA dictionary definition of 銅雀臺].}}{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.32 }}: {{lang|zh|"[十五年]冬，作銅爵臺。"}} In January 211, Cao Cao wrote a long memorial – to the throne as well as to a more general audience including his detractors – declining to accept three counties awarded to him by Emperor Xian to be part of his marquisate, in which he also wrote at length about his life and ambitions.{{efn|This early example of autobiographical writing, often called Cao Cao's ''Apologia'', can be read translated in full as part of an open-access book chapter.{{Cite book| editor1= Ebrey, Patricia Buckley | editor2= Cong Ellen Zhang | editor3= Ping Yao | chapter= Military Men Touting Their Merits: Essays by Cao Cao 曹操 (155–220) and His Son Cao Pi 曹丕 (187–226) | title= Chinese Autobiographical Writing: An Anthology of Personal Accounts | pages= 59–66 | publisher=University of Washington Press | date= 2023 | jstor=j.ctv369c5z3.14| isbn= 9780295751221 }}}} In the spring of 211, Emperor Xian appointed Cao Cao's son, [[Cao Pi]], as General of the Household for All Purposes ({{lang|zh|五官中郎將}}). Cao Pi had his own office and served as an assistant to his father, the Imperial Chancellor.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34 }}: {{lang|zh|"十六年春正月，天子命公世子丕為五官中郎將，置官屬，為丞相副。"}} At the same time, in accordance with Cao Cao's wishes in the essay he wrote earlier, Emperor Xian reduced the number of taxable households in Cao Cao's marquisate by 5,000, and granted the three counties to three of Cao Cao's sons – [[Cao Zhi]], [[Cao Ju (Prince of Pengcheng)|Cao Ju]] and [[Cao Lin (Prince of Pei)|Cao Lin]]{{efn|The ''Sanguozhi'' erroneously recorded his name as Cao Bao {{nowrap|({{lang|zh|曹豹}})}}, the Marquis of Raoyang ({{lang|zh|饒陽侯}}). It should be Cao Lin.}} – who were enfeoffed as marquises.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"庚辰，天子報：減戶五千，分所讓三縣萬五千封三子，植為平原侯，據為范陽侯，豹為饒陽侯，食邑各五千戶。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34 n. 1 }}. Sometime in early 211, Shang Yao ({{lang|zh|商曜}}) from [[Taiyuan|Taiyuan Commandery]] started a rebellion in Daling County ({{lang|zh|大陵縣}}; north of present-day [[Wenshui County]], Shanxi). Cao Cao sent [[Xiahou Yuan]] and [[Xu Huang]] to lead an army to suppress the revolt and they achieved success.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34 }}: {{lang|zh|"太原商曜等以大陵叛，遣夏侯淵、徐晃圍破之。"}} ==Battle of Tong Pass (211–213)== [[File:Cao exp200-220.png|200px|thumb| {{Legend|#0000FF|Cao Cao's territory in 206}} {{Legend|RoyalBlue|Cao Cao's conquests 207–215}} {{Legend|LimeGreen|Other warlords}}]] {{main|Battle of Tong Pass}} In early 211, Cao Cao ordered [[Zhong Yao]] and [[Xiahou Yuan]] to lead an army to attack [[Zhang Lu (Han dynasty)|Zhang Lu]] in [[Hanzhong|Hanzhong Commandery]]. They were due to pass through the [[Guanzhong]] region along the way. The warlords in Guanzhong thought that Cao Cao was planning to attack them, so they, under the leadership of [[Ma Chao]] and [[Han Sui]], formed a coalition known as the Guanxi Coalition ({{lang|zh|關西軍}}; "coalition from the west of [[Tong Pass]]") and rebelled against the Han imperial court.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34}}: {{lang|zh|"張魯據漢中，三月，遣鍾繇討之。公使淵等出河東與繇會。是時關中諸將疑繇欲自襲，馬超遂與韓遂、楊秋、李堪、成宜等叛。"}} A few months later, Cao Cao personally led a campaign against the rebels and engaged them in battle in the areas around Tong Pass (in present-day [[Tongguan County]], Shaanxi) and the banks of the [[Wei River]]. The first engagement took place when Cao Cao's forces were crossing the Wei River to the north bank, during which they suddenly came under attack by Ma Chao. Cao Cao and his forces headed back to the south bank later, where they constructed sand walls to keep the enemy at bay.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34 }}: {{lang|zh|"公自潼關北渡，未濟，超赴船急戰。校尉丁斐因放牛馬以餌賊，賊亂取牛馬，公乃得渡，循河爲甬道而南。"}} After some time, the rebels offered to cede territories and send a hostage to Cao Cao's side in exchange for peace. Acting on [[Jia Xu]]'s suggestion, Cao Cao pretended to accept the offer to put the enemy at ease and make them lower their guard. Cao Cao later had talks with Han Sui (an old acquaintance of his) on at least two different occasions. The first time was a private conversation between them about old times, while the second time probably took place in the presence of Ma Chao and the other coalition members. Ma Chao and the others started to doubt Han Sui's allegiance,{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"公後日復與遂等會語，諸將曰：「公與虜交語，不宜輕脫，可為木行馬以為防遏。」公然之。 ...又列鐵騎五千為十重陣，精光耀日，賊益震懼。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.36 n. 4 }}. especially after Han Sui received a letter from Cao Cao which contained several blotted-out words, making it seem as though the recipient had deliberately edited the letter's contents to cover up something. Cao Cao took advantage of the mutual suspicion between the rebels to launch an attack on them and defeated them. Some of the warlords were killed in battle while Han Sui and Ma Chao retreated back to Guanzhong.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.34–35}}: {{lang|zh|"九月，進軍渡渭。 ...超等數挑戰，又不許；固請割地，求送任子，公用賈詡計，偽許之。 ...韓遂請與公相見，公與遂父同歲孝廉，又與遂同時儕輩，於是交馬語移時，不及軍事，但說京都舊故，拊手歡笑。旣罷，超等問遂：「公何言？」遂曰：「無所言也。」超等疑之。 ...他日，公又與遂書，多所點竄，如遂改定者；超等愈疑遂。公乃與克日會戰，先以輕兵挑之，戰良久，乃縱虎騎夾擊，大破之，斬成宜、李堪等。遂、超等走涼州，楊秋奔安定，關中平。"}} ===Aftermath=== Cao Cao returned to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei) in late 211 after receiving the surrender of one of the remaining warlords, [[Yang Qiu (warlord)|Yang Qiu]]. He left [[Xiahou Yuan]] behind to defend [[Chang'an]], a major city in the [[Guanzhong]] region. [[Ma Chao]], who had the support of the [[Qiang (historical people)|Qiang]], [[Di (Wu Hu)|Di]] and other tribal peoples in western China, continued to ravage Guanzhong and attack Cao Cao's territories. In 213, he killed [[Wei Kang]], the Inspector of [[Liang Province]], [[Siege of Jicheng|seized control of the province]], and forced Wei Kang's subordinates to submit to him. In late 213, Zhao Qu ({{lang|zh|趙衢}}), Yin Feng ([[:zh:尹奉|尹奉]]) and several other officials in Liang Province [[Battle of Lucheng|rebelled against Ma Chao]] and drove him out of Guanzhong. With aid from [[Zhang Lu (Han dynasty)|Zhang Lu]], Ma Chao returned and struck back at his enemies, but was defeated when Xiahou Yuan led reinforcements from Chang'an to assist Zhao Qu and his allies. Xiahou Yuan later attacked the remnants of the Guanxi Coalition (including [[Han Sui]]) and the various tribes in western China and forced them to surrender. He also eliminated Song Jian ([[:zh:宋建|宋建]]), who had rebelled against the Han government and set up a small kingdom in Fuhan County ({{lang|zh|枹罕縣}}; southwest of present-day [[Linxia County]], [[Gansu]]).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.36 }}: {{lang|zh|"冬十月，軍自長安北征楊秋，圍安定。秋降... 十二月，自安定還，留夏侯淵屯長安。... 馬超餘衆梁興等屯藍田，使夏侯淵擊平之。"}}{{pb}}{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.42 }}: {{lang|zh|"馬超在漢陽，復因羌、胡為害，氐王千萬叛應超，屯興國。使夏侯淵討之。十九年春正月... 南安趙衢、漢陽尹奉等討超，梟其妻子，超奔漢中。韓遂徙金城，入氐王千萬部，率羌、胡萬餘騎與夏侯淵戰，擊，大破之，遂走西平。淵與諸將攻興國，屠之。省安東、永陽郡。"}}{{pb}}{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.44 }}: {{lang|zh|"初，隴西宋建自稱河首平漢王，聚衆枹罕，改元，置百官，三十餘年。遣夏侯淵自興國討之。冬十月，屠枹罕，斬建，涼州平。"}} ==Wars with Sun Quan (213–217)== {{main|Battle of Ruxu (213)|Battle of Ruxu (217)}} In early 213, Cao Cao led an army to attack Sun Quan at Ruxu ({{lang|zh|濡須}}; north of present-day [[Wuwei County]], Anhui, along the Yangtze River). During the battle, Cao Cao's forces destroyed Sun Quan's camp on the west bank of the Yangtze and captured Gongsun Yang ({{lang|zh|公孫陽}}), an area commander under Sun Quan. However, overall, both sides did not make any significant gains in the battle.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.37 }}: {{lang|zh|"[十七年]冬十月，公征孫權。十八年春正月，進軍濡須口，攻破權江西營，獲權都督公孫陽，乃引軍還。"}} In mid-214, Cao Cao launched another campaign against Sun Quan against the advice of [[Fu Gan]], one of his advisers. Just like in the previous campaign, he did not make any significant gains so he retreated. In the following year, Sun Quan led his forces to attack Hefei, a heavily fortified city guarded by Cao Cao's generals [[Zhang Liao]], [[Li Dian]] and [[Yue Jin]], leading to the [[Battle of Xiaoyao Ford]]. Zhang Liao and the defenders inflicted a devastating defeat on Sun Quan and his forces.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.43–45 }}: {{lang|zh|"[十九年]秋七月，公征孫權。 ...公自合肥還。 ...[二十年]八月，孫權圍合肥，張遼、李典擊破之。"}} In the winter of 216, Cao Cao staged a military drill in [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei), during which he personally beat a war drum to direct his troops' movements and boost their morale.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"王親執金鼔以令進退。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.49 n. 1 (first n. 1)}}. After the drill, he launched another campaign against Sun Quan and arrived in Juchao ({{lang|zh|居巢}}; in present-day [[Chaohu]], Anhui) by spring in the following year. In late March or April 217, he ordered his troops to make camp at the Hao Gorge ({{lang|zh|郝谿}}) on the west bank of the Yangtze. Sun Quan had constructed a dock and stationed defences at Ruxu. Both sides clashed at Ruxu and the battle ended with an inconclusive result. Cao Cao withdrew his forces in late April or May 217, leaving behind [[Xiahou Dun]], [[Cao Ren]], Zhang Liao and others to defend Juchao.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.49}}: {{lang|zh|"[二十一年]冬十月，治兵，遂征孫權，十一月至譙。二十二年春正月，王軍居巢，二月，進軍屯江西郝谿。權在濡須口築城拒守，遂逼攻之，權退走。三月，王引軍還，留夏侯惇、曹仁、張遼等屯居巢。"}} ==Campaign against Zhang Lu (215)== {{main|Battle of Yangping}} In early 215, Cao Cao launched a campaign against [[Zhang Lu (Han dynasty)|Zhang Lu]] in Hanzhong Commandery. He first sent [[Zhang He]], [[Zhu Ling (Three Kingdoms)|Zhu Ling]] and others to lead an army to attack the [[Di (Wu Hu)|Di tribes]] blocking the way in Wudu Commandery ([[:zh:武都郡#漢代武都郡|武都郡]]; around present-day [[Longnan]], Gansu). They defeated and massacred the Di population in Hechi County ({{lang|zh|河池縣}}; northwest of present-day [[Pingliang]], Gansu).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.45 }}: {{lang|zh|"[二十年]三月，公西征張魯，至陳倉，將自武都入氐；氐人塞道，先遣張郃、朱靈等攻破之。夏四月，公自陳倉以出散關，至河池。氐王竇茂衆萬餘人，恃險不服，五月，公攻屠之。西平、金城諸將麴演、蔣石等共斬送韓遂首。"}} By mid 215, Cao Cao's army reached Yangping Pass ({{lang|zh|陽平關}}; in present-day [[Ningqiang County]], [[Shaanxi]]) after making a long and arduous journey across mountainous terrain. When his soldiers started complaining, Cao Cao announced that he would remember them for their contributions to encourage them to move on.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"軍自武都山行千里，升降險阻，軍人勞苦；公於是大饗，莫不忘其勞。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.45 n. 2 }}. Zhang Lu ordered his younger brother Zhang Wei ([[:zh:張衛|張衛]]) and subordinate Yang Ang ([[:zh:楊昂|楊昂]]) to lead troops to defend the pass, making use of the mountainous terrain to counter Cao Cao's advances. Cao Cao was unable to overcome the enemy after launching assaults so he withdrew to put them off guard. One night, Cao Cao secretly ordered Xie Biao ({{Lang|zh|解𢢼}}) and Gao Zuo ([[:zh:高祚|高祚]]) to lead a sneak attack on Yangping Pass. Zhang Lu retreated to [[Bazhong]], when he heard that Yangping Pass had been taken. Cao Cao proceeded to occupy [[Nanzheng County]], the capital of Hanzhong Commandery.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.45 }}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，公至陽平。張魯使弟衞與將楊昂等據陽平關，橫山築城十餘里，攻之不能拔，乃引軍還。賊見大軍退，其守備解散。公乃密遣解忄剽、高祚等乘險夜襲，大破之，斬其將楊任，進攻衞，衞等夜遁，魯潰奔巴中。公軍入南鄭，盡得魯府庫珍寶。"}} After taking control of Hanzhong Commandery, Cao Cao made some administrative changes to the commandery, such as redrawing boundaries and appointing some administrators to govern the newly formed commanderies. In late 215, Zhang Lu led his followers out of Bazhong and voluntarily submitted to Cao Cao, who accepted his surrender and granted him a marquis title. Around the time, Liu Bei had recently [[Liu Bei's takeover of Yi Province|seized control of Yi Province]] (present-day Sichuan and Chongqing) from its governor [[Liu Zhang (warlord)|Liu Zhang]] and occupied Bazhong after Zhang Lu left. Cao Cao ordered Zhang He to lead a force to attack Liu Bei, but Zhang He lost to Liu Bei's general [[Zhang Fei]] at the [[Battle of Baxi]]. About a month after Zhang Lu's surrender, Cao Cao left Nanzheng County and headed back to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei), leaving behind [[Xiahou Yuan]] to guard Hanzhong Commandery.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.45–46 }}: {{lang|zh|"巴、漢皆降。復漢寧郡為漢中；分漢中之安陽、西城為西城郡，置太守；分錫、上庸郡，置都尉。 ...九月，巴七姓夷王朴胡、賨邑侯杜濩舉巴夷、賨民來附，於是分巴郡，以胡為巴東太守，濩為巴西太守，皆封列侯。天子命公承制封拜諸侯守相。 ...十一月，魯自巴中將其餘衆降。封魯及五子皆為列侯。劉備襲劉璋，取益州，遂據巴中；遣張郃擊之。十二月，公自南鄭還，留夏侯淵屯漢中。"}} ==War with Liu Bei in Hanzhong (217–219)== {{main|Hanzhong Campaign}} In the winter of 217, Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, [[Ma Chao]], Wu Lan ([[:zh:吳蘭|吳蘭]]) and others to garrison at Xiabian ({{lang|zh|下辯}}; northwest of present-day [[Cheng County]], Gansu). Cao Cao ordered [[Cao Hong]] to lead an army to resist the enemy. In the spring of 218, Cao Hong defeated Wu Lan and killed his deputy Ren Kui ([[:zh:任夔|任夔]]). In April or May 218, Zhang Fei and Ma Chao retreated from Hanzhong Commandery while Wu Lan was killed by Qiangduan ([[:zh:強端|強端]]), a [[Di (Wu Hu)|Di]] chieftain from Yinping Commandery ({{lang|zh|陰平郡}}; around present-day [[Wen County, Gansu]]).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.50–51 }}: {{lang|zh|"[二十二年冬] 劉備遣張飛、馬超、吳蘭等屯下辯；遣曹洪拒之。二十三年春... 曹洪破吳蘭，斬其將任夔等。三月，張飛、馬超走漢中，陰平氐強端斬吳蘭，傳其首。"}} In August or early September 218, Cao Cao staged a military drill and launched a campaign against Liu Bei. His army reached [[Chang'an]] in October. In the meantime, Liu Bei's forces had already engaged Cao Cao's forces, under [[Xiahou Yuan]]'s command, in Hanzhong Commandery. In early 219, Xiahou Yuan was killed in action at the [[Battle of Mount Dingjun]] against Liu Bei's general [[Huang Zhong]]. In April 219, Cao Cao led his forces from Yangping Pass ({{lang|zh|陽平關}}; in present-day [[Ningqiang County]], Shaanxi) towards Hanzhong via Xie Valley ({{lang|zh|斜谷}}). Liu Bei made use of the geographical advantage he had – mountainous terrain – to hold off Cao Cao.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.51–52 }}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，治兵，遂西征劉備，九月，至長安。 ...夏侯淵與劉備戰於陽平，為備所殺。三月，王自長安出斜谷，軍遮要以臨漢中，遂至陽平。備因險拒守。"}} That July, Cao Cao withdrew his forces back to Chang'an.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.52 }}: {{lang|zh|"夏五月，引軍還長安。"}} ==Battle of Fancheng (219–220)== {{Main|Battle of Fancheng}} In the autumn of 219, Cao Cao ordered [[Yu Jin]] to lead seven armies to reinforce Cao Ren, who was under siege by Guan Yu at Fancheng. However, due to heavy rains, the [[Han River (Hubei and Shaanxi)|Han River]] burst its banks and the seven armies were destroyed in the flood. Guan Yu captured Yu Jin, executed his subordinate [[Pang De]], and continued to press on the attack on Cao Ren. Cao Cao ordered [[Xu Huang]] to lead another army to help Cao Ren.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.52 }}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月， ...遣于禁助曹仁擊關羽。八月，漢水溢，灌禁軍，軍沒，羽獲禁，遂圍仁。使徐晃救之。"}} At the same time, Cao Cao also contemplated relocating the imperial capital from [[Xuchang]] further north into Hebei to avoid Guan Yu, but [[Sima Yi]] and [[Jiang Ji]] told him that [[Sun Quan]] would become restless when he heard of Guan Yu's victory. They suggested to Cao Cao to ally with Sun Quan and enlist his help in hindering Guan Yu's advances. In return, Cao Cao would recognise the legitimacy of Sun Quan's claim over the territories in Jiangdong. In this way, the siege on Fancheng would automatically be lifted. Cao Cao heeded their suggestion.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|36}}.941 }}: {{lang|zh|"曹公議徙許都以避其銳，司馬宣王、蔣濟以為關羽得志，孫權必不願也。可遣人勸權躡其後，許割江南以封權，則樊圍自解。曹公從之。"}} Cao Cao arrived in Luoyang early in the winter of 219 after returning from campaign in Hanzhong. He later led an army from Luoyang to relieve Cao Ren, but turned back before reaching his destination upon receiving news that Xu Huang had defeated Guan Yu and lifted the siege on Fancheng.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.52 }}: {{lang|zh|"冬十月，軍還洛陽。 ...孫權遣使上書，以討關羽自效。王自洛陽南征羽，未至，晃攻羽，破之，羽走，仁圍解。王軍摩陂。"}} In the spring of 220, Cao Cao returned to Luoyang and remained there. In the meantime, Sun Quan had sent his general [[Lü Meng]] and others to [[Lü Meng's invasion of Jing Province|launch a stealth assault]] on Liu territories in [[Jing Province]] while Guan Yu was on the Fancheng campaign, and they succeeded in conquering Guan Yu's key bases in [[Gong'an County]] and [[Jiangling County]]. Guan Yu, having lost his bases and forced to withdraw from Fancheng, was eventually surrounded by Sun Quan's forces and captured in an ambush and executed. Sun Quan sent Guan Yu's head to Cao Cao,{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.53 }}: {{lang|zh|"二十五年春正月，至洛陽。權擊斬羽，傳其首。"}} who arranged a noble's funeral for Guan Yu and had his head buried with full honours.Hu Chong, ''Wu Li'': {{lang|zh|"權送羽首於曹公，以諸侯禮葬其屍骸。}}" Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|36}}.942 n. 3 }}. ==Titles of nobility (213–220)== ===Duke of Wei=== Cao Cao returned to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] in the spring of 212 after the Battle of Tong Pass. [[Emperor Xian of Han|Emperor Xian]] granted him special privileges similar to those awarded to [[Xiao He]] by [[Emperor Gaozu of Han|Emperor Gao]]. Cao Cao did not have to have his name announced, did not have to walk in quickly, and had permission to carry a ceremonial sword and wear shoes when he entered the imperial court. Fourteen counties from five different commanderies were segregated from their respective commanderies and placed under the jurisdiction of [[Wei Commandery]] (around present-day Handan, Hebei).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.36}}: {{lang|zh|"[建安]十七年春正月，公還鄴。天子命公贊拜不名，入朝不趨，劔履上殿，如蕭何故事。 ...割河內之蕩陰、朝歌、林慮，東郡之衞國、頓丘、東武陽、發干，鉅鹿之廮陶、曲周、南和，廣平之任城，趙之襄國、邯鄲、易陽以益魏郡。"}} The 1st month of the 17th year of ''Jian'an'' corresponds to 20 Feb to 20 Mar 212 in the Julian calendar. In 213, after Cao Cao returned from the [[Battle of Ruxu (213)|Battle of Ruxu]] against [[Sun Quan]], Emperor Xian issued a decree abolishing the fourteen provinces system and replacing it with an older [[Nine Provinces (China)|nine provinces]] system. About a month after Cao Cao returned to Ye, Emperor Xian sent [[Chi Lü]] as an emissary to enfeoff Cao Cao as the Duke of Wei ({{lang|zh|魏公}}). After Cao Cao refused the customary three times, the emperor sent a thirty-person delegation of officials to make a fourth offer of enfeoffment, which was accepted.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"前後三讓。於是中軍師陵樹亭侯荀攸...等勸進... 公乃受命。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.40–41 n. 9}}. In August 213, an [[ancestral temple]] and the [[Soil and grain|''sheji'' (altars for worshipping the gods of soil and grain)]] were built in Cao Cao's dukedom. Later, Emperor Xian sent a six-person delegation led by high ranking government minister Wang Yi ([[:zh:王邑 (東漢)|王邑]]) to present betrothal gifts of jade, silk, and other precious items to Cao Cao as part of an arrangement for three of Cao Cao's daughters to become the emperor's concubines: [[Empress Cao Jie|Cao Jie]], Cao Hua, and Cao Xian.''Xiandi qiju zhu'': {{lang|zh|"使使持節行太常大司農安陽亭侯王邑，齎璧、帛、玄纁、絹五萬匹之鄴納娉，介者五人，皆以議郎行大夫事，副介一人。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.42 n. 1}}.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.37}}: {{lang|zh|"十八年春正月... 詔書幷十四州，復為九州。夏四月，至鄴。五月丙申，天子使御史大夫郗慮持節策命公為魏公"}}.{{pb}}{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.42}}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，始建魏社稷宗廟。天子娉公三女為貴人，少者待年于國。"}} It is to be understood that these grants of honours, titles, prerogatives, and imperial marriage arrangements were not of the emperor's own initiative, but orchestrated by Cao Cao and his staff, who controlled the Imperial Secretariat. As early as the ''[[Book of the Later Han]]'', few historians offer Cao Cao the veneer of legitimacy in his appointments and enfeoffments, forgoing mention of the emperor and instead describing the actions as a personal decision.{{sfnp|de Crespigny|2010|p=472}} In October 213, Cao Cao ordered the construction of the Golden Tiger Platform ({{lang|zh|金虎臺}}) and a watercourse linking the [[Zhang River]] and White Canal ({{lang|zh|白溝}}). A month later, he divided Wei Commandery into the east and west divisions, each governed by a Commandant. In December, he established a ducal secretariat in his fief along with the offices of Palace Attendants and the Six Ministers.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.42}}: {{lang|zh|"九月，作金虎臺，鑿渠引漳水入白溝以通河。冬十月，分魏郡為東西部，置都尉。十一月，初置尚書、侍中、六卿。"}} [[File:Imperial Encyclopaedia - Ceremonial Usages - pic369 - 遠遊冠.svg|153px|thumb|Depiction of a ''yuanyou guan'', an authoritative hat granted to Cao Cao by [[Emperor Xian of Han|Emperor Xian]]]] In late January or February 214, Cao Cao attended a ceremony, known as ''ji li'' ({{lang|zh|籍禮}}), to promote agriculture.{{efn|In ancient China, emperors and nobles would recruit peasants to help them work their personal farming plots. The emperor owned 1,000 [[Chinese units of measurement#Area|''mu'']] of land while a noble owned 100 ''mu''. The ''ji li'' ({{lang|zh|籍禮}}) was a ceremony during which the emperor or the noble would use a plow to lift the soil three times or turn the soil over once. This was a symbolic move to show that the emperor or noble was concerned about agriculture and served as a role model for peasants to follow.}}{{cite encyclopedia | chapter= Definition of 籍田 | chapter-url= https://www.zdic.net/hant/%E7%B1%8D%E7%94%B0 | title = zdic 漢典 | language= zh}} In late March or April, Emperor Xian sent Yang Xuan ({{lang|zh|楊宣}}) and Pei Mao ([[:zh:裴茂 (東漢)|裴茂]]) as emissaries''Xiandi qiju zhu'': "使左中郎將楊宣、亭侯裴茂持節、印授之。 Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.43 n. 1 (second n. 1)}}. to present Cao Cao with a golden official seal with a red ribbon and a ''yuanyou guan'' ({{lang|zh|遠遊冠}}),{{efn|A ''yuanyou guan'' ({{lang|zh|遠遊冠}}) was a type of ceremonial headgear. Cao Cao is depicted wearing a ''yuanyou guan'' in the picture in the infobox above.}} placing Cao (who was still only a duke then) in a position above other nobles.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.42–43}}: {{lang|zh|"十九年春正月，始耕籍田。 ...[十九年]三月，天子使魏公位在諸侯王上，改授金璽，赤紱、遠遊冠。"}} In December 214 or January 215, Empress [[Fu Shou]] wrote a secret letter to her father Fu Wan ([[:zh:伏完|伏完]]) to tell him that Emperor Xian resented Cao Cao for the execution of [[Dong Cheng (Han dynasty)|Dong Cheng]]. The contents of the letter were hateful. The incident was exposed and Empress Fu was deposed and executed, her family exiled.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.44}}: {{lang|zh|"[十九年]十一月，漢皇后伏氏坐昔與父故屯騎校尉完書，云帝以董承被誅怨恨公，辭甚醜惡，發聞，后廢黜死，兄弟皆伏法。"}} In January or February 215, Cao Cao went to Meng Ford ({{lang|zh|孟津}}), a historically important spot near the site of the ancient [[Battle of Muye]]. Emperor Xian allowed him to make a ''maotou'' ({{lang|zh|旄頭}}; a banner decorated with animals' tails, typically reserved for the emperor) and erect a ''zhongju'' ({{lang|zh|鍾虡}}; a bell pendant stand) in his ducal palace. Cao Cao later issued two official statements and established a ''licaoyuan'' ({{lang|zh|理曹掾}}; a justice ministry).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.44}}: {{lang|zh|"十二月，公至孟津。天子命公置旄頭，宮殿設鍾虡。...於是置理曹掾屬。"}} In the spring of 215, Emperor Xian instated Cao Cao's daughter, [[Empress Cao Jie|Cao Jie]], as the new empress. Cao Cao visited four commanderies and merged them into a new commandery – Xinxing Commandery ({{zh|labels=no|c=新興郡|l=The Newly Rising Commandery}}) – with one of the counties as the commandery capital. In winter, while he was away in Hanzhong Commandery, Cao Cao created the titles of the Five Counsellors and nominal marquis titles for the first time, alongside the original six grades of marquis ranks.{{efn|There were 18 grades for nominal marquis titles and 17 grades for ''guanzhong'' marquises; holders of these titles each had a golden seal with a purple ribbon attached. There were 16 grades for ''guannei'' ({{lang|zh|關內}}) and ''guanwai'' ({{nowrap|{{lang|zh|關外}}}}) marquises; holders of these titles each had a bronze seal with a handle carved in the shape of a tortoise and with a black ribbon attached. There were 15 grades for the Five Counsellors; holders of these titles each had a bronze seal with a handle carved in the shape of a jade ring and with a black ribbon attached. All the bearers of these titles did not have any fiefs with taxable households; they possessed only honorary titles. These new titles were created in addition to the preexisting marquises ranks which were divided into six grades.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"置名號侯爵十八級，關中侯爵十七級，皆金印紫綬；又置關內外侯十六級，銅印龜紐墨綬；五大夫十五級，銅印環紐，亦墨綬，皆不食租，與舊列侯關內侯凡六等。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.46 n. 1 (second n. 1)}}. The historian [[Pei Songzhi]] believed that Cao Cao started the practice of conferring honorary titles in the late Eastern Han dynasty,Pei Songzhi in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.46 n. 1 (second n. 1)}}: {{lang|zh|"臣松之以為今之虛封蓋自此始。"}} but see also [[Ranged Marquis]].}} These new titles were awarded to Cao Cao's men who had made contributions in battle during the campaign against Zhang Lu, as Cao Cao had promised them earlier.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.45–46}}: {{lang|zh|"二十年春正月，天子立公中女為皇后。省雲中、定襄、五原、朔方郡，郡置一縣領其民，合以為新興郡。 ...[二十年]冬十月，始置名號侯至五大夫，與舊列侯、關內侯凡六等，以賞軍功。"}} In February or early March 216, Cao Cao returned to [[Ye (ancient China)|Ye]] (present-day [[Handan]], Hebei) after [[Battle of Yangping|a successful campaign]] against [[Zhang Lu (Han dynasty)|Zhang Lu]] in Hanzhong Commandery.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.47}}: {{lang|zh|"二十一年春二月，公還鄴。"}} Two months later, he attended another ''ji li'' ({{lang|zh|籍禮}}) ceremony.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.47}}: {{lang|zh|"三月壬寅，公親耕籍田。"}} ===King of Wei=== In June 216, Emperor Xian promoted Cao Cao from a duke to a [[vassal]] king under the title "King of Wei" ({{lang|zh|魏王}}). Cao Cao summoned [[Sima Fang]], who had recommended him to be the Commandant of the North District in Luoyang early in his career, to meet him in Ye, where they had a chat.{{efn|See [[Sima Fang#Relationship with Cao Cao]] for details.}} Later, the [[Wuhuan]] chanyu Pufulu ({{lang|zh|普富盧}}) from Dai Commandery ({{lang|zh|代郡}}; northwest of present-day [[Yu County, Hebei]]) led his various subjects to Ye to pay tribute to Cao Cao. Around the same time, Emperor Xian instated one of Cao Cao's daughters as a princess and granted her a fief with some taxable households. In August 216, the Southern [[Xiongnu]] chanyu [[Huchuquan]] brought along his subjects to pay tribute to Cao Cao, who treated them like guests. Huchuquan remained in Cao Cao's vassal kingdom while the former Southern Xiongnu domain in [[Bingzhou|Bing province]] was reorganized into the "Five Divisions" ({{lang|zh|五部}}) and placed under the supervision of Huchuquan's uncle, [[Qubei]]. In September, Cao Cao promoted [[Zhong Yao]] from the position of Grand Judge ({{lang|zh|大理}}) under the Han central government to the Royal Chancellor ([[:zh:相國#中國|相國]]) of his vassal kingdom.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.47}}: {{lang|zh|"夏五月，天子進公爵為魏王。代郡烏丸行單于普富盧與其侯王來朝。天子命王女為公主，食湯沐邑。秋七月，匈奴南單于呼廚泉將其名王來朝，待以客禮，遂留魏，使右賢王去卑監其國。八月，以大理鍾繇為相國。"}} He also established the offices of the Minister of Ancestral Ceremonies ([[:zh:太常|奉常]]) and Minister of the Royal Clan ([[:zh:宗正|宗正]]) in his vassal kingdom.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"始置奉常宗正官。"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.49 n. 4}}. In late May or June 217, Emperor Xian allowed Cao Cao to have his personal ''jingqi'' ({{lang|zh|旌旗}}; a banner) and have imperial guards clear the path when Cao travelled around. In late June or July, Cao Cao had a ''pangong'' ({{lang|zh|泮宮}}){{efn|A ''pangong'' ({{lang|zh|泮宮}}) was an educational institution for the sons of nobles and aristocrats.}} constructed. In July or August, [[Hua Xin]] was appointed as Imperial Counsellor ([[:zh:御史大夫|御史大夫]]). Cao Cao also established the office of the Minister of the Guards ([[:zh:衞尉|衞尉]]) in his vassal kingdom.{{harvnb|Book of Wei}}: {{lang|zh|"初置衞尉官。}}" Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.49 n. 1 (second n. 1)}}. In November or December, Emperor Xian granted more ceremonial privileges to Cao Cao: have twelve fringes of pearls on his crown; ride in a golden carriage pulled by six horses; have five other carriages to accompany his main carriage when he travelled around. Cao Cao's son, [[Cao Pi]], who was serving as General of the Household for All Purposes ({{lang|zh|五官中郎將}}) in the Han imperial court, was designated as the Crown Prince ({{lang|zh|太子}}) of Cao Cao's vassal kingdom.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.49}}: {{lang|zh|"[二十二年]夏四月，天子命王設天子旌旗，出入稱警蹕。五月，作泮宮。六月，以軍師華歆為御史大夫。冬十月，天子命王冕十有二旒，乘金根車，駕六馬，設五時副車，以五官中郎將丕為魏太子。"}} In February or early March 218, the imperial physician [[Ji Ben]], along with Geng Ji ([[:zh:耿紀|耿紀]]), Wei Huang ([[:zh:韋晃|韋晃]]) and others, started a rebellion in the imperial capital [[Xuchang]] and attacked the camp of Wang Bi ([[:zh:王必|王必]]), a chief clerk under Cao Cao. Wang Bi suppressed the revolt with the aid of Yan Kuang ([[:zh:嚴匡|嚴匡]]), an Agriculture General of the Household ({{lang|zh|典農中郎將}}).{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.50}}: {{lang|zh|"二十三年春正月，漢太醫令吉本與少府耿紀、司直韋晃等反，攻許，燒丞相長史王必營，必與潁川典農中郎將嚴匡討斬之。"}} In late July or August 219, Cao Cao designated his formal spouse, [[Empress Dowager Bian|Lady Bian]], as his queen consort.{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.52}}: {{lang|zh|"秋七月，以夫人卞氏為王后。"}} Some months later, Sun Quan wrote to Cao Cao, expressing his desire to submit to Cao Cao and urging Cao Cao to take the throne from Emperor Xian. Cao Cao showed Sun Quan's letter to his subordinates and remarked: "This kid wants me to put myself on top of a fire!" [[Chen Qun]], [[Huan Jie]] and [[Xiahou Dun]] also urged Cao Cao to usurp the imperial throne from Emperor Xian, but Cao Cao refused.{{harvnb|Yu|265}}: {{lang|zh|"孫權上書稱臣，稱說天命。王以權書示外曰：「是兒欲踞吾著爐火上邪！」侍中陳羣、尚書桓階奏曰：「漢自安帝已來，政去公室，國統數絕，至於今者，唯有名號，尺土一民，皆非漢有，期運久已盡，歷數久已終，非適今日也。是以桓、靈之閒，諸明圖緯者，皆言『漢行氣盡，黃家當興』。殿下應期，十分天下而有其九，以服事漢，羣生注望，遐邇怨歎，是故孫權在遠稱臣，此天人之應，異氣齊聲。臣愚以為虞、夏不以謙辭，殷、周不吝誅放，畏天知命，無所與讓也。」"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.52–53 n. 2}}.[[Sun Sheng (Jin dynasty)|Sun Sheng]], {{harvnb|Wei Shi Chunqiu}}: {{lang|zh|"夏侯惇謂王曰：「天下咸知漢祚已盡，異代方起。自古已來，能除民害為百姓所歸者，即民主也。今殿下即戎三十餘年，功德著於黎庶，為天下所依歸，應天順民，復何疑哉！」王曰：「『施于有政，是亦為政』。若天命在吾，吾為周文王矣。」"}} Cited in {{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.53 n. 2}}. ==Death and burial (220)== Cao Cao died on 15 March 220 in Luoyang at the age of 66 (by [[East Asian age reckoning]]). He was granted the [[Posthumous name|posthumous title]] "King Wu" ({{lang|zh|武王}}; "martial king") by Emperor Xian. His will instructed that he be buried near [[Ximen Bao]]'s tomb in Ye without gold and jade treasures, and that his subjects on duty at the frontier were to stay in their posts and not attend the funeral as, in his own words, "the country is still unstable".{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.53}}: {{lang|zh|"遺令曰：「天下尚未安定，未得遵古也。葬畢，皆除服。其將兵屯戍者，皆不得離屯部。有司各率乃職。斂以時服，無藏金玉珍寶。」"}} He was buried on 11 April 220 in the Gaoling ({{lang|zh|高陵}}; "high mausoleum").{{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|1}}.53}}: "庚子，王崩于洛陽，年六十六。 ...謚曰武王。二月丁卯，葬高陵。" In December 220 or early January 221, after Cao Pi forced Emperor Xian to abdicate the throne in his favour and established the state of [[Cao Wei]], he granted his father the posthumous title "Emperor Wu" ({{lang|zh|武皇帝}}; "Martial Emperor"){{harvnb|Chen and Pei|429|loc={{strong|2}}.76}} and the [[temple name]] "Taizu" ({{lang|zh|太祖}}; "Grand Ancestor").{{harvnb|Zizhi Tongjian|1084|loc=volume {{strong|69}}}}: {{lang|zh|"十一月，癸酉，奉漢帝為山陽公，行漢正朔，用天子禮樂；封公四子為列侯。追尊太王曰太皇帝；武王曰武皇帝，廟號太祖；尊王太后曰皇太后。"}} ===Cao Cao Mausoleum=== [[File:20250913 Gao Mausoleum of Cao Cao 01.jpg|thumb|The [[Cao Cao Mausoleum]] Museum in [[Anyang County|Anyang]], Henan]] {{main|Cao Cao Mausoleum}} On 27 December 2009, the Henan Provincial Cultural Heritage Bureau reported the discovery of Cao Cao's tomb in Xigaoxue Village, [[Anyang County]], Henan. The tomb, covering an area of 740 square metres, was discovered in December 2008 when workers at a nearby kiln were digging for mud to make bricks. Its discovery was not reported and the local authorities knew of it only when they seized a stone tablet carrying the inscription 'King Wu of Wei' – Cao Cao's posthumous title – from grave robbers who claimed to have stolen it from the tomb. Over the following year, archaeologists recovered more than 250 relics from the tomb. The remains of three persons – a man in his 60s, a woman in her 50s and another woman in her 20s – were also unearthed.{{cite web |author=Lin Shujuan |title=Tomb of legendary ruler unearthed |url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/china/2009-12/28/content_9234640.htm |publisher=China Daily |access-date=28 July 2023 |date=28 December 2009}} Since the discovery of the tomb, there have been many sceptics and experts who pointed out problems with it and raised doubts about its authenticity.{{cite web |author=Zhang Zhongjiang (张中江) |script-title=zh:学者称曹操墓葬确认在河南安阳证据不足 | title=Experts say there is insufficient evidence to confirm that Cao Cao's tomb is in Anyang, Henan |url=https://news.sina.cn/sa/2009-12-29/detail-ikftpnny4231728.d.html |publisher=Tengxun News |access-date=28 July 2023 |language=zh |date=29 December 2009}} In January 2010, the [[State Administration of Cultural Heritage]] legally endorsed the initial results from research conducted throughout 2009 suggesting that the tomb was Cao Cao's.{{cite web |author=Wang Yun (王荟) |script-title=zh:国家文物局认定河南安阳东汉大墓墓主为曹操 | title=SACH confirms that the Eastern Han tomb in Anyang, Henan belonged to Cao Cao |url=http://news.ppzw.com/article_Show_157147.html |publisher=Tengxun News |access-date=28 July 2023 |language=zh |date=29 January 2010}} However, in August 2010, 23 experts and scholars presented evidence at a forum held in [[Suzhou, Jiangsu|Suzhou]] to argue that the findings and the artefacts of the tomb were fake.{{cite web |author=Jiang Wanjuan |title=Cao Cao's tomb: Experts reveal that findings and artifacts are fake |url=http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/90001/90782/90873/7114984.html |publisher=Global Times |date=24 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110913163753/http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/90001/90782/90873/7114984.html |archive-date=13 September 2011 |url-status=dead}} In 2010, archaeologist Zhang Guo'an published a book positing that the tomb and the adjacent one actually belonged to [[Cao Huan]] (a grandson of Cao Cao) and his father [[Cao Yu (Three Kingdoms)|Cao Yu]].{{multiref2|{{cite book|last= Zhang |first= Guo'an | author-mask= Zhang Guo'an (张国安) | script-title=zh:顛覆曹操墓 |publisher=Dongfang Chubanshe |place=Anyang| date=2010 |isbn= 9787506039123| language=zh}}|Cited in {{cite news|date=21 June 2010 | script-title=zh:学者颠覆曹操高陵定论:墓主人应是末代皇帝曹奂 | url= https://www.chinanews.com.cn/cul/news/2010/06-21/2353697.shtml | publisher=Chinanews| language =zh| author=Chen Jingxia (陈菁霞)}} }} With the release of the formal archaeological report about the tomb in 2016, the academic community had moved on from the identity debate and went on to study the tomb with the understanding that it does indeed belong to Cao Cao.{{Cite book |last=Zhou |first=Ligang |title=Hun gui Ye xi : Cao Cao Gaoling yan jiu |publisher=[[China Science Publishing]] |year=2024 |isbn=7030782240 |location=Beijing |language=zh-hans |script-title=zh:魂归邺西 : 曹操高陵研究|pages=93–95}} In 2010, the tomb became part of the fifth batch of [[Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level|Major Historical and Cultural Sites Protected at the National Level]] in China.{{cite web |author=Yang Yuguo (杨玉国) |script-title=zh:河南曹操高陵少林寺入选全国重点文物保护单位 |title=Henan's Cao Cao Mausoleum and Shaolin Monastery are selected to be Major Historical and Cultural Sites Protected at the National Level |url=http://gb.cri.cn/42071/2013/05/03/3245s4104173.htm|publisher=CRI online |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504110025/http://gb.cri.cn/42071/2013/05/03/3245s4104173.htm |archive-date=4 May 2014 |url-status=dead |language=zh |date=3 May 2013}} A museum was opened at the site in April 2023.{{cite news | author2= Yang Zhitian (杨之甜) | author1= Xie Jianxiao (谢建晓) | work= Henan Daily | date= 28 April 2023 | url= https://hct.henan.gov.cn/2023/04-28/2734585.html | via= Henan Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230728224145/https://hct.henan.gov.cn/2023/04-28/2734585.html | archive-date= 28 July 2023 | script-title= zh:安阳曹操高陵遗址博物馆开馆 | title= Anyang Cao Cao Gaoling Archaeological Site Museum opens | url-status= live }} ==Family== {{further|Cao Wei family trees}} According to historical records, Cao Cao had 15 wives and concubines, 25 sons, six daughters and two adopted sons. His first formal spouse was Lady Ding, who raised his eldest son [[Cao Ang]] (born to his concubine Lady Liu). She fell out with him after Cao Ang's death and effectively separated from him. After Lady Ding left him, Cao Cao designated [[Empress Dowager Bian|Lady Bian]], one of his concubines, as his new formal spouse and she remained in this position permanently. Among Cao Cao's sons (excluding Cao Ang), the more notable ones are [[Cao Pi]], [[Cao Zhang]], [[Cao Zhi]] and [[Cao Chong]], who were, at different points in time, considered as potential candidates to succeed their father. Cao Chong, who was born to Lady Huan, was a [[child prodigy]] who devised a method of weighing an elephant by using the principle of buoyancy. Cao Chong died prematurely at the age of 12. Cao Pi, Cao Zhang and Cao Zhi were born to Lady Bian and were known for their individual talents: Cao Pi and Cao Zhi were noted as brilliant writers and poets; Cao Zhang inherited his father's military skills. Cao Pi eventually overcame his two younger brothers in a succession struggle and was chosen to be his father's heir apparent.
