After being defeated and the Star self-destructed, he used a dagger to kill himself so that he could die in his own home rather than spend his life in the Vatican dungeons. As he lay dying on the floor, he offered Esther the chance to take her vengeance for Bishop Laura, but she refused and instead comforted him in place of his wife until he died.<ref name="Ep4" />

Tritoma | colspan=2 {{dunno}} |- ! rowspan=2 | 13 years BCT – present ! rowspan=2 | [[#Boa Hancock|Boa Hancock]] | [[#Boa Sandersonia|Boa Sandersonia]] || |- | [[#Boa Marigold|Boa Marigold]] || |} The {{nihongo|'''Kuja Pirates'''|九蛇海賊団|Kuja Kaizokudan}} are a crew formed by members of the [[Kuja Tribe]], and captained by their empress, [[#Boa Hancock|Boa Hancock]]. They are a crew formed by the strongest fighters of the Kuja, including Hancok's two younger sisters who possess the Zoan-type abilities of the {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit|ヘビヘビの実|Hebi Hebi no Mi}} branch.{{gnr|ch|519}} The Boa sisters are known as the "Gorgon Sisters", being based on the three [[Gorgons]] of the [[Greek mythology]], while the members of the crew are based on the [[Amazons]].{{cite web |url=https://www.animeherald.com/2024/01/13/one-piece-keeps-greek-mythology-alive-with-boa-hancock/ |title=One Piece Keeps Greek Mythology Alive With Boa Hancock |author= Caitlin Sinclair Chappell |date=January 13, 2024 |website=Anime Herald}} ====Boa Hancock==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Hancock'''|ボア・ハンコック|Boa Hankokku}} is a member of the all-female [[Kuja Tribe]] from the island of Amazon Lily.{{gnr|ch|515|f.}} Sold to the [[World Government (One Piece)#Celestial Dragons|Celestial Dragons]] during childhood, she and her sisters are force-fed devil fruits and [[Human branding|branded]] as slaves.{{gnr|ch|521}} Eventually freed by [[#Fisher Tiger|Fisher Tiger]], the three return to their people. Hancock becomes ruler and is referred to by her subjects as {{nihongo|"'''Snake Princess'''"|蛇姫|Hebihime}}.{{gnr|ch|516|, |521}} Leading the Kuja Pirates, she quickly gains infamy as the {{nihongo|"'''Pirate Empress'''"|海賊女帝|Kaizoku Jotei}} and is offered membership in the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|516|, |522}} Despite resenting the World Government for her past enslavement, which she keeps a secret even from her kinswomen, Hancock accepts the position to protect her people. But when called upon to participate in the Government's war against the [[Whitebeard Pirates]], she initially refuses and only reconsiders after falling in love with [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]], who enlists her help to infiltrate [[Impel Down]].{{gnr|ch|516|f., |520|–|522}} The ability of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Love-Love Fruit|メロメロの実|Mero Mero no Mi}} allows her to turn anyone charmed by her into stone and back again, with the sole exception of Luffy due to his lack of any sexual interest in her.{{gnr|ch|516|, |521}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/strong-female-devil-fruit-users/ |title=15 Strongest Female Devil Fruit Users In One Piece |author=Kara Ketchum |date=June 21, 2023|website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} Her fruit's abilities can also be countered by forcing yourself to feel another emotion that drowns out your lust, for example pain, as shown when Vice Admiral Momonga avoided being turned to stone by stabbing himself in the hand. She is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. After the most recent Reverie, the Seven Warlords were disbanded, making her an enemy of the World Government again. In the Japanese anime television series, her voice actress is [[Kotono Mitsuishi]].{{cite video |year=2011 |title=One Piece: 12thシーズン 女ヶ島篇: Piece.01 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} In the Funimation English adaptation, her voice is supplied by [[Lydia Mackay]]. Her abilities are based on those of the Gorgon [[Medusa]] in [[Greek mythology]]. =====Salome===== {{nihongo|'''Salome'''|サロメ|Sarome}} is Boa Hancock's pet snake who supports her in battle, and also acts as her throne that she sits on. He is white with patches of red. He wears a skull upon his head. ====Boa Sandersonia==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Sandersonia'''|ボア・サンダーソニア|Boa Sandāsonia}} is the middle sister whose {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit: Model Anaconda|ヘビヘビの実 モデル アナコンダ|Hebi Hebi no Mi: Moderu Anakonda}} enables her to transform into an [[anaconda]] or anaconda-human hybrid. Boa Sandersonia is voiced by [[Chiwa Saitō]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Lindsay Seidel]] in the Funimation dub. ====Boa Marigold==== {{nihongo|'''Boa Marigold'''|ボア・マリーゴールド|Boa Marīgōrudo}} is the youngest sister whose {{nihongo|Snake-Snake Fruit: Model King Cobra|ヘビヘビの実 モデル キングコブラ|Hebi Hebi no Mi: Moderu Kingu Kobura}} enables her to turn into a [[king cobra]] or king cobra-human hybrid. Boa Marigold is voiced by [[Kimiko Saitō]] in the original Japanese version and by Julie Mayfield in the Funimation dub. ===={{visible anchor|Shakky|Shakuyaku}}==== {{nihongo|'''Shakuyaku'''|シャクヤク}}, most commonly known by her nickname "'''Shakky'''", was the Empress and captain of the Kuja Pirates after Gloriosa. Her extreme popularity in comparison to Gloriosa led to her eventually taking over the post, but nevertheless retires to open a bar on Fullalead.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1156|,|1158}} Her kidnapping by the World Government led to the God Valley Incident.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1159}} Both the [[#Rocks Pirates|Rocks Pirates]] and the [[#Roger Pirates|Roger Pirates]] arrived where they each wanted to rescue her.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1160}} After the Roger Pirates disband, she marries [[#Silvers Rayleigh|Silvers Rayleigh]] and works as a bartender at Sabaody Archipelago. Shakuyaku is voiced by [[Hiromi Tsuru]] in the original Japanese version, [[Masumi Asano]] in Episode 870 of the original Japanese version, and by [[Elizabeth Maxwell]] in the Funimation dub. ====Gloriosa==== {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Gloriosa}}'''|グロリオーサ|Guroriōsa}}, more commonly referred to as "'''Elder Nyon'''", is a short elderly woman who was the Empress of Amazon Lily and the captain of the Kuja Pirates approximately 60 years before current events. Roger]], only to leave behind her post and subsequently the country after his rejection in favor of Shakuyaku.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1156}} Gloriosa is voiced by [[Ako Mayama]] in the original Japanese version and by Nancy Sherrand in the Funimation dub. ====Other Kuja pirates==== * {{nihongo|'''Marguerite'''|マーガレット|Māgaretto}}: A warrior who befriends Luffy. Oars is voiced by [[Mayumi Tanaka]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Colleen Clinkenbeard]] in the Funimation dub. ===Sun Pirates=== {{see also|Jimbei|#Fisher Tiger}} [[File:Sun Pirates Jolly Roger.svg|thumb|200px|The Sun Pirates' Jolly Roger, an alteration of the Hoof of the Soaring Dragon.]] The {{nihongo|'''Sun Pirates'''|タイヨウの海賊団|Taiyō no Kaizokudan}} are a band of pirates consisting of fish-men and [[Merman|mermen]] that was originally led by [[#Fisher Tiger|Fisher Tiger]] and later by [[Jimbei]]. They attack any pirate ship they see, but no matter who is on it, they never kill directly.{{gnr|ch|622}} Their Sun insignia was created to cover up the mark of the Celestial Dragon's slave, "Hoof of the Soaring Dragon", since many on the crew bore the mark from being enslaved. The Sun insignia was designed to completely cover the Hoof branding, so the World Government was unable to know which crew member to kidnap and re-enslave due confusion over their former status.{{gnr|ch|620}} The members of the [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]] and [[#Macro Pirates|Macro Pirates]] were also members of the crew.{{gnr|ch|622}} The Sun Pirates temporarily shelter a human child, [[Koala (One Piece)|Koala]], who escaped from Marijoa during Tiger's liberation,{{gnr|ch|622}} and eventually return her to her parents on Foolshout Island, where a Marine ambush led by Rear Admiral Strawberry results in Tiger's death.{{gnr|ch|623}} With Arlong imprisoned, Jimbei took over the Sun Pirates until he joined the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]]; as part of Jimbei's conditions for accepting the role, which he believes will bring Queen Otohime's dream closer to reality, Arlong is released, but he and the rest of the Arlong Pirates leave the crew, as well as the members of the Macro Pirates.{{gnr|ch|624}} The Sun Pirates later served under Big Mom as her subordinates, until Jinbe decided to abandon their alliance with her. They helped the Straw Hats escape from Big Mom's territory.{{cite web|url=http://books.shueisha.co.jp/CGI/search/syousai_put.cgi?isbn_cd=978-4-08-881496-4|title=One Piece/89|publisher=Shueisha|access-date=May 17, 2018|language=ja|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523205807/http://books.shueisha.co.jp/CGI/search/syousai_put.cgi?isbn_cd=978-4-08-881496-4|archive-date=May 23, 2018|url-status=live}}{{cite book|title=One Piece/89|publisher=Viz Media|isbn=1974705218}} The current known members of the Sun Pirates are: * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Aladine}}'''|アラディン|Aradin}}: A [[Brotula multibarbata|goatsbeard brotula]]-type merman who is the crew's doctor and first mate during Jimbei's leadership. Aladine was once enslaved and is now married to Charlotte Praline. Aladine is voiced by [[Takashi Nagasako]] in the original Japanese version and by Brad Smeaton in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Charlotte Praline}}'''|シャーロット・プラリネ|Shārotto Purarine}}: Aladine's wife and [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]]'s 21st daughter who is a hybrid of a human and a hammerhead shark-type merman. She is the younger twin sister of [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Charlotte Prim|Charlotte Prim]]. Charlotte Praline is voiced by Yuko Tachibana in the original Japanese version and by Sara Ragsdale in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Wadatsumi}}'''|ワダツミ}}: A giant [[Takifugu rubripes|tiger blowfish]]-type fish-man who is a former member of the [[#New Fish-Man–Flying Pirates Alliance|Flying Pirates]]. It also enables him to control sharp thin strings from his fingertips that can cut people, create clones of himself, and attach to the clouds in the sky to allow him to fly.{{gnr|ch|231}} He is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. He is also a former Celestial Dragon after his father, Donquixote Homing, decided to abandon that life to become a normal human. However, they were chased by the people, tortured, and eventually Doflamingo killed his father. He brought the head of his father back to Mariejois in hopes of receiving his Celestial title back again. He was denied and later became a pirate. He believes that the "Great Pirate Era" is nearing its end and a new age is about to begin.{{gnr|ch|303}} He is a [[broker]] under the alias of "{{visible anchor|Joker}}", and owns a large auction house at the Sabaody Archipelago, where humans and other species are sold as slaves.{{gnr|ch|504}} Eventually after the Straw Hat Crew and Dressrosa's citizens reveal his treacherous deeds, Doflamingo is defeated by Luffy and his title is revoked leading to the arrest of him and his pirate crew. He is voiced by [[Hideyuki Tanaka]].{{cite video |year=2004 |title=6thシーズン 空島·スカイピア篇: Piece.03 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} In the Funimation English adaptation, his voice is supplied by [[Robert McCollum]].{{cite video |year=2010 |title=One Piece: Season 3: First Voyage |medium=DVD |publisher=Funimation Entertainment |isbn=978-1-4210-2119-5 }} ====Elite Officers==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Trébol}}'''|トレーボル|Torēboru}}: The leader of the [[#Trébol Army|Trébol Army]], occupying the Club seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], with the powers of the Stick-Stick Fruit (ベタベタの実, Beta Beta no Mi) which allows him to generate an adhesive and highly sticky liquid. Trébol is voiced by [[Taiki Matsuno]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Alejandro Saab]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Diamante}}'''|ディアマンテ}}: The leader of the [[#Diamante Army|Diamante Army]], occupying the Diamond seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], who has the powers of the Ripple-Ripple Fruit (ヒラヒラの実, Hira Hira no Mi) which allows him to flatten, reform, and fold anything while still retaining its original characteristics. Diamante is voiced by [[Hideyuki Umezu]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Brad Hawkins (actor)|Brad Hawkins]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Pica}}'''|ピーカ|Pīka}}: The leader of the [[#Pica Army|Pica Army]], occupying the Spade seat of [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], and a large, muscular man with a comically high voice with the powers of the Stone-Stone Fruit (イシイシの実, Ishi Ishi no Mi), which allows him to absorb, manipulate, and merge with stone. Pica is voiced by [[Yūji Mitsuya]] in the original Japanese version and by Ry McKeand in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Vergo}}'''|ヴェルゴ|Berugo}}: A tall, light-skinned, lean, yet muscular man who is an elite officer of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]], formerly occupying the Heart seat and went by the code name "Corazon" before [[#Donquixote Rosinante|Rosinante]], undercover as a [[Marines (One Piece)|Naval vice admiral]] heading G-5 in Punk Hazard. He is a practitioner of Rokushiki and is also proficient in the use of Armament Haki. After being defeated by [[#Trafalgar Law|Law]], he dies when the SAD Production Room explodes he was in. Vergo is voiced by [[Junichi Suwabe]] in the original Japanese version and by Wes Frazierin the Funimation dub. ====Donquixote Pirates' Officers==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Trébol Army}}'''|トレーボル軍|Torēboru-gun}} is a division of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]] led by [[#Trébol|Trébol]] specializing in missions that require users with special powers.{{gnr|ch|732}} Its officers consists of: ** {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Sugar}}'''|シュガー|Shugā}}: A girl ranked as a "special officer" of the Trébol Army with the powers of the Hobby-Hobby Fruit (ホビホビの実, Hobi Hobi no Mi), which allows her to turn people into [[toy]]s. Sugar is voiced by [[Rie Kugimiya]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Natalie Hoover]] in the Funimation. ** {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Giolla}}'''|ジョーラ|Jōra}}: A woman with the powers of the Art-Art Fruit (アトアトの実, Ato Ato no Mi) which allows her to transform things into [[modern art]]. Giolla is voiced by [[Hiroko Emori]] in the original Japanese version and by CJ Critt in the Funimation dub. ** '''[[List of One Piece characters#Viola|Viola]]''', under the code name {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Violet}}'''|ヴィオラ|Baioretto}}, was also part of the Trébol Army. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Diamante Army}}'''|ディアマンテ軍|Diamante-gun}}: A division of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]] led by [[#Diamante|Diamante]] specializing in fighting missions.{{gnr|ch|732}} Its officers consists of: ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Lao G}}'''|ラオ・G|Rao Jī}}: An old skilled martial artist obsessed with the letter G. Lao G is voiced by [[Tetsuo Gotō]] in the original Japanese version and by Jim White in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Machvise}}'''|マッハバイス|Mahhabaisu}}: A strong man with the powers of the Ton-Ton Fruit (トントンの実, Ton Ton no Mi) which allows him to change his weight at will. Machvise is voiced by [[Naomi Kusumi]] in the original Japanese version and by Shawn Gann in the Funimation dub. ** {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Senor Pink}}'''|セニョール・ピンク|Senyōru Pinku}}: A "hard boiled" man with the power of the Swim-Swim Fruit (スイスイの実, Sui Sui no Mi) which allows him to swim through the ground or walls. He primarily fights with kicks. Her bird parts were the replacements for her original parts. Monet was killed when Caesar accidentally stabbed her removed heart instead of Smoker's removed heart. Monet is voiced by [[Naoko Matsui]] in the original Japanese version and by Janelle Lutz in the Funimation dub. ===Hanafuda=== "King of Lizards" {{nihongo|'''Hanafuda'''|ハナフダ}} was a former Warlord of the Sea. He is the father of [[Ulti (One Piece)|Ulti]] and [[Page One (One Piece)|Page One]] and entrusted them to [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] after agreeing to serve the Animal Kingdom Pirates. He used to collect Ancient Zoan Devil Fruits. After he was defeated by [[Portgas D. Ace]], Hanafuda was stripped of his title and replaced by Bartholomew Kuma. He was later killed by a rival pirate. Doflamingo replaced Hanafuda's relationship with the Animal Kingdom Pirates.{{gnr|vol|111|:SBS}} ===Bartholomew Kuma=== The {{nihongo|"'''Tyrant'''"|暴君|Bōkun}} {{nihongo|'''Bartholomew Kuma'''|バーソロミュー・くま|Bāsoromyū Kuma|{{nihongo||[[wikt:熊|熊]]|kuma}} meaning [[bear]]}}, is one of the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]]; the only one with a reputation for complete obedience to the World Government, when in fact he is an officer of the [[List of One Piece characters#Revolutionary Army|Revolutionary Army]].{{gnr|ch|234|, |473|f., |603}} He was formerly a slave with Emporio Ivankov and Ginny, saving others at the God Valley incident before escaping. He later became the King of the Sorbet Kingdom, raising Jewelry Bonney, Ginny's daughter, from childhood.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1098}} The power of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Paw-Paw Fruit|ニキュニキュの実|Nikyu Nikyu no Mi}} allows his palms to repel anything, from physical objects such as people or air to abstracts such as pain and fatigue.{{gnr|ch|484|f.}} He can use this ability to safely transport himself or others over long distances.{{gnr|ch|514}} Kuma is the model for the {{anchor|Pacifista}}{{nihongo|Pacifista|パシフィスタ|Pashifisuta}}, a class of experimental cyborgs created by Dr. Vegapunk for the Government. Their bodies are made of a substance harder than steel, and they can shoot powerful blasts from their mouths that can melt metal.{{gnr|ch|485}} The other Pacifista look just like Kuma, sharing his towering, bear-like stature, but lack the Paw-Paw Fruit's ability. Instead, they are able to shoot laser beams based on Admiral Kizaru's Glint-Glint Fruit laser abilities from their palms.{{gnr|ch|508|f.}} At some point during his gradual conversion into the human weapon {{anchor|PX-0}}"PX-0", Kuma's personality is erased, leaving him a programmable fighting machine under the Government's control until becoming a slave-to-rent for the World Nobles as punishment for aiding Luffy.{{gnr|ch|559|f.}} However, parts of his personality gradually returned as he unexpectedly ran across the Grand Line to Egghead to save Bonney, enough to recognize her and attack Jaygarcia Saturn; he became a companion of the Straw Hat Crew on their escape, arriving on Elbaph with them. Teach|Blackbeard]], eventually became known as the {{nihongo|"'''Worst Generation'''"|最悪の世代|Saiaku no Sedai}} by the World Government as they gained more notoriety for their crimes and, sometimes, their willingness to challenge the [[status quo]].{{gnr|ch|664}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-worst-generation-bounty-ranked/ |title=One Piece: Every Worst Generation Member's Bounty, Ranked From Lowest to Highest |author=Rylie Clothier |date=August 2, 2025 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} ===Basil Hawkins=== {{nihongo|'''Basil Hawkins'''|バジル・ホーキンス|Bajiru Hōkinsu}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Magician'''"|魔術師|Majutsushi}}, is the captain of the {{visible anchor|Hawkins Pirates}}, originating from the North Blue. He ate the {{nihongo|Straw-Straw Fruit|ワラワラの実|Wara Wara no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to create and manipulate straw. He can cover himself in straw and make [[scarecrow]]-like straw avatars to aid his offense.{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/unique-one-piece-devil-fruits/ |title=What Are The Most Unique Devil Fruit Powers in One Piece? |author=Christian Markle |date=August 9, 2023 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} He also has a habit of reading tarot cards to find out what is going to happen and the percentage probability that what he predicts will happen. After the two year timeskip, he tried to form an alliance with [[#Scratchmen Apoo|Scratchmen Apoo]] and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]. After [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] appeared in front of them, he ended up joining the [[Animal Kingdom Pirates]] as Kaido's subordinate, betraying Kid along with Apoo, and becoming one of the crew's Headliners. During the battle on Onigashima, he ended up facing [[#Killer|Killer]], ultimately being defeated by him. Basil Hawkins is voiced by [[Shigenori Sōya]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Taliesin Jaffe]] in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life buccaneer [[Basil Ringrose]] and the privateer [[John Hawkins (naval commander)|John Hawkins]].{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-characters-based-on-real-people/ |title=One Piece Characters Based On Historical Figures |date=October 24, 2024 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} ===Capone Bege=== {{nihongo|'''Capone''' "'''Gang'''" '''Bege'''|カポネ・“ギャング”・ベッジ|Kapone "Gyangu" Bejji}} is a [[Crime boss|mafia don]] turned pirate. He has the power of the {{nihongo|Castle-Castle Fruit|シロシロの実|Shiro Shiro no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to create and maintain a dimensional fortress inside his body, being able to put people inside after being reduced when approaching the entrances of his body, or transforming into a great castle that serves as a fortress.{{gnr|ch|812}} During the two year time skip, Bege became one of the [[Big Mom Pirates]]' combatants until he formed an alliance with Luffy and [[Caesar Clown]] to finish off Big Mom. Bege is married to [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]] and they are both the parents of {{nihongo|Capone Pez|カポネ・ペッツ|Kapone Pettsu}}. Capone Bege is voiced by [[Naoki Tatsuta]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Kyle Hebert]] in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life gangster [[Al Capone]]. ===={{visible anchor|Fire Tank Pirates|Firetank Pirates}}==== The {{nihongo|'''Fire Tank Pirates'''|ファイアタンク海賊団|Faia Tanku Kaizokudan}} are Capone Bege's pirate crew, originating from the West Blue. Later on, they incorporate the Rolling Pirates into their crew. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Vito}}'''|ヴィト}}: Nicknamed {{nihongo|"Phantom Gun"|怪銃|Kaijū|{{lit}} "Monster Gun"}}, is Bege's advisor.{{gnr|ch|813}} Vito is voiced by [[Daisuke Kishio]] in the original Japanese version and by Chris Hackney in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Gotti}}'''|ゴッティ}}: Bege's combatant.{{gnr|ch|825}} He is married to [[#Charlotte Lola|Charlotte Lola]] of the Rolling Pirates.{{gnr|ch|993}} Gotti is voiced by [[Masafumi Kimura]] in the original Japanese version and by Joshua Passmore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Charlotte Chiffon}}'''|シャーロット・シフォン|Shārotto Shifon}}: Is Bege's wife, and they are both the parents of Capone Pez. She is [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]]'s 22nd daughter, as well as [[#Pound|Pound]]'s daughter, and Charlotte Lola's twin sister. Chiffon is voiced by [[Aya Hisakawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Kate Bristol]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Charlotte Lola}}'''|シャーロット•ローラ|Shārotto Rōra}}: Captain of the Rolling Pirates. She and her crew were among the victims of [[#Gecko Moria|Gecko Moria]] in Thriller Bark. She is the 23rd daughter of [[Charlotte Linlin|Big Mom]] and twin sister of [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]]. Lola ran away from Totto Land when her mother wanted her to marry [[Loki (One Piece)|Prince Loki]] of Elbaph, deciding to sail in the sea to find someone she truly loved. During her trip, she asked all the men she met if they wanted to marry her, eventually marrying [[#Gotti|Gotti]] in a merging of the Fire Tank Pirates and the Rolling Pirates.{{gnr|ch|993}} Lola is voiced by [[Aya Hisakawa]] in the original Japanese version and by Alex Moore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Risky Brothers}}'''|リスキー兄弟|Risukī Kyōdai}}: Two Rolling Pirates crew members who keep track of all the times their Lola has been rejected by the men. The tallest of the duo is voiced by Yūsuke Numata in the original Japanese version and by Brandon Jerome Bristowe in the Funimation dub, while the shortest of the duo is voiced by Tamotsu Nishiwaki in the original Japanese version and by Ian Moore in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Pound}}'''|パウンド|Paundo}}: A 24 ft. human who is the 25th ex-husband of Big Mom and the father of [[#Charlotte Chiffon|Charlotte Chiffon]] and [[#Charlotte Lola|Charlotte Lola]]. After he was discarded by Big Mom, Pound worked to reunite with his daughters which led to his encounter with the Straw Hat Crew. Though he got burned rescuing Chiffon's group from [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Charlotte Oven|Charlotte Oven]],{{gnr|ch|887}} he was later found adrift by the [[Tontatta Pirates]] and was taken to Dressrosa to be healed.{{gnr|ch|979}} Pound later proved to Chiffon and Lola that he was their father when he saved their ship from an attack by a Marine ship.{{gnr|ch|989}} The Fire Tank Pirates pulled him aboard. Pound later attended the wedding of Lola and [[#Gotti|Gotti]].{{gnr|ch|993}} Pound is voiced by [[Masami Kikuchi]] in the original Japanese version and by Patrick McAllister in the Funimation dub. ===Jewelry Bonney=== {{nihongo|'''Jewelry Bonney'''|ジュエリー・ボニー|Juerī Bonī}} is one of twelve pirates collectively known as the [[#Worst Generation|Worst Generation]] and the only female of the group. She is nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Glutton'''"|大喰らい|Ō-Gurai|{{lit.}} "Big Eater"}} because of her gigantic appetite which, however, does not affect her sinuous figure.{{gnr|ch|498}} She has eaten the Age-Age Fruit, which allows her to change her own age (which she uses to disguise herself) as well as others, making her opponents either too young or too old to fight her; despite her appearance, she is a 12-year-old child. She is the captain of the Bonney Pirates, mostly consisting of fishermen acquainted with her.{{gnr|ch|499}} Born to Revolutionary [[List of One Piece characters#Ginny|Ginny]] and a World Noble, she was raised by [[Bartholomew Kuma]] from childhood, making her princess of the [[List of One Piece characters#Sorbet Kingdom|Sorbet Kingdom]] during Kuma's reign.{{Gnr|ch|1100}} After the Paramount War, she and her crew were defeated and captured by the [[Blackbeard Pirates]], and she was subsequently arrested by the [[Marines (One Piece)|Marine]] fleet led by [[Sakazuki (One Piece)|Sakazuki]]. Somehow, she managed to escape, showing herself wandering the streets incognito after the two year timeskip. During the World Meeting, she infiltrated Marijoa to rescue Kuma, eventually catching up to the Straw Hats at Egghead for similar matters. Jewelry Bonney is voiced by [[Reiko Kiuchi]] and later by [[Reiko Takagi]] in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, she is voiced by Laura Wetsel. The character is named after the real life pirate [[Anne Bonney]].{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/one-piece-real-life-pirates-inspired-characters/ |title=One Piece: 10 Real Pirates That Inspired The Characters' Creation |author=Caleb Greenough |date=June 14, 2022 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}} ===Kid Pirates=== ====Eustass Kid==== {{nihongo|'''Eustass''' "'''Captain'''" '''Kid'''|ユースタス・キャプテン・キッド|Yūsutasu "Kyaputen" Kiddo}} is the captain of the {{visible anchor|Kid Pirates}}, originating from the South Blue. Among his crew is his childhood friend [[#Killer|Killer]]. Kid ate the {{nihongo|Magnet-Magnet Fruit|ジキジキの実|Jiki Jiki no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows him to attract and control metal objects with magnetism.{{gnr|vol|99|:SBS}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/one-piece-devil-fruits-function-water/ |title=10 One Piece Devil Fruits That Can Still Work In Water |author=George Voutiritsas |date=February 21, 2025 |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]]}} He is also capable of utilizing all three types of Haki. During the time skip, he lost his arm after an encounter with [[Shanks (One Piece)|Shanks]], depending on a metal pieces arm created by his ability. After trying to form an alliance with [[#Scratchmen Apoo|Scratchmen Apoo]] and [[#Basil Hawkins|Basil Hawkins]], he ended up being betrayed by them and captured by [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], having to later ally himself with [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] and [[#Trafalgar Law|Law]] in their plan to defeat him. After the events at Wano, Kid's whereabouts are currently unknown after another failed attempt to assault Shanks. Eustass Kid is voiced by [[Daisuke Namikawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Justin Cook]] in the Funimation dub. Both his name and epithet are based in the real life privateer [[William "Captain" Kidd]]. ====Killer==== {{nihongo|'''Killer'''|キラー|Kirā}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Murder Machine'''"|殺戮武人|Satsuriku Bujin|{{lit}} "Massacre Soldier"}} is the combatant of the Kid Pirates and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]'s childhood friend. He usually fights using two blades, and stands out for wearing a mask on his face. After he and Kid were captured by [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], Killer was forced to eat a dud SMILE fruit, leaving him permanently smiling. In [[Wano Country|Wano]], he ended up working for Kaido's ally [[Kurozumi Orochi]] as a street assassin known as {{nihongo|Kamazo the Manslayer|人斬り鎌ぞう|Hito Kiri Kamazō}}. To get revenge on Kaido, he and the Kid Pirates ended up joining [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] and [[World Government (One Piece)#Trafalgar Law|Law]]'s alliance. Killer is voiced by [[Kenji Hamada]] in the original Japanese version and by Leo Fabian in the Funimation dub. ===Scratchmen Apoo=== {{nihongo|'''Scratchmen Apoo'''|スクラッチメン・アプー|Sukuratchimen Apū}}, also known as {{nihongo|"'''Roar of the Sea'''"|海鳴り|Umi Nari}}, is the captain of the {{nihongo|On-Air Pirates|オンエア海賊団|On Ea Kaizokudan}}, and a member of the longarm tribe. He has the power of the {{nihongo|Tone-Tone Fruit|オトオトの実|Oto Oto no Mi}}, a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that gives him the ability to transform parts of his body into various instruments and generate music and great vibrations with them, however, sound does not affect people if they do not hear it. After the two year timeskip, he tried to form an alliance with [[#Basil Hawkins|Basil Hawkins]] and [[#Eustass Kid|Eustass Kid]]. However, he was affiliated with [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]] to ambush them with Apoo being actually a subordinate of the [[Animal Kingdom Pirates]] as their informant, ending up with Hawkins joining Kaido and Apoo, and Kid being captured. Scratchmen Apoo is voiced by [[Mitsuaki Madono]] in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, he is voiced by Brad Venable in episodes 392-629 and ''One Piece: Stampede'' and by Brent Mukai starting in Episode 736. The character is named after the real life pirate [[Chui A-poo]]. ===Trafalgar Law=== The {{nihongo|"'''Surgeon of Death'''"|死の外科医|Shi no Gekai}}, {{nihongo|'''Trafalgar D. Water Law'''|トラファルガー・D・ワーテル・ロー|Torafarugā Dī Wāteru Rō}}, originates from the North Blue.{{gnr|ch|498|, |508|, |578|, |763}} Having eaten the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Op-Op Fruit|オペオペの実|Ope Ope no Mi}}, Law can, after generating a blue spherical area around himself, cut and teleport objects as well as perform [[body swap]]s within said blue area.{{gnr|ch|661}} He is the captain of the Heart Pirates. Originally from the White Town, Flevance, he escaped with White Lead Disease and became a member of the [[#Donquixote Pirates|Donquixote Pirates]]. There he met Donquixote Rosinante, the brother of Doflamingo, and together they went on an adventure to find a cure for Law. Ultimately they found the Devil Fruit, but before they escaped, Rosinante was killed by Doflamingo, leaving Law to seek out revenge. Law makes a name for himself and following the Paramount War, Law joins the [[Seven Warlords of the Sea]].{{gnr|ch|659|, |673}} Though he enters into an alliance with Luffy and the Straw Hats to take down [[Kaido (One Piece)|Kaido]], one of the Four Emperors, Law is actually hunting down [[#Donquixote Doflamingo|Donquixote Doflamingo]].{{cite web |url=https://mein-mmo.de/en/the-5-most-loyal-allies-of-luffy-in-one-piece-who-are-not-crew-members,1242875/ |title=The 5 most loyal allies of Luffy in One Piece who are not crew members - Trafalgar Law |author=Esmeralda Eickemeyer |date=March 31, 2025 |website=mein-mmo.de}} Law's whereabouts are unknown after a devastating defeat against the Blackbeard Pirates, though he survived due to crew member and polar bear Bepo's interference. Trafalgar Law is voiced by [[Hiroshi Kamiya]] in the original Japanese version{{cite video |year=2011 |title=One Piece: 11thシーズン シャボンディ諸島篇: Piece.04 |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} and by [[Matthew Mercer]] in the Funimation dub. The character's name takes inspiration after the real life pirate [[Edward Low]], as well as from the historical battles of [[Battle of Trafalgar|Trafalgar]] and [[Battle of Waterloo|Waterloo]]. ====Heart Pirates==== The {{nihongo|'''Heart Pirates'''|ハートの海賊団|Hāto no Kaizokudan}} is the pirate crew led by Trafalgar Law, consisting of twenty-one members, including: * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Bepo}}'''|ベポ}}: A [[polar bear]]-type [[Mink Tribe|mink]] and crew navigator. Bepo is voiced by [[Yasuhiro Takato]] in the original Japanese version and by Cris George in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Shachi}}'''|シャチ}}: An average-size lean man who wears an orca-shaped hat. Shachi is voiced by Takahiro Fujimoto in the original Japanese version and by Ben Bryant in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Penguin}}'''|ペンギン|Pengin}}: An average-size lean man who wears a hat with his name on it. Penguin is voiced by Keiji Hirai in the original Japanese version and by Seth Magill in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Jean Bart}}'''|ジャンバール|Janbāru}}: A large man who was a former slave of Saint Rosward. Jean Bart is voiced by [[Yasunori Masutani]] in the original Japanese version and by John McCalmont in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life privateer [[Jean Bart]]. ===Urouge=== {{nihongo|'''Urouge'''|ウルージ|Urūji}}, nicknamed the {{nihongo|"'''Mad Monk'''"|怪僧|Kaisō}}, is the high priest of the Mad Monk Pirates.{{gnr|ch|498}} He is originally from some Sky Island. Urouge ate an unidentified Devil Fruit that allows him to increase his muscle mass, expanding his muscles and enlarged body size.{{gnr|ch|508}} Urougue is voiced by Taiten Kusunoki in the original Japanese version and by Major Attaway in the Funimation dub. ===X. Drake=== {{main|World Government (One Piece)#X. Drake|l1=World Government (''One Piece'') § X. Drake}} ==Roger Pirates== The {{nihongo|'''Roger Pirates'''|ロジャー海賊団|Rojā Kaizokudan}} were the pirate crew of the late King of the Pirates, [[#Gol D. Roger|Gol D. Roger]], and were the only known crew to ever reach Laugh Tale. [[Shanks (One Piece)|Shanks]] and [[Buggy the Clown|Buggy]] started out as cabin boys on the crew. Because the Samurai [[Kozuki Oden]] could read the Poneglyphs, he, alongside his wife [[Kozuki Toki|Toki]], children [[Kozuki Momonosuke|Momonosuke]] and [[Kozuki Hiyori|Hiyori]], as well as his retainers [[Dogstorm and Cat Viper]], accompanied Roger and his crew for one year to learn the secrets of the world (such as the Void Century, ancient weapons, and the D. Family), as well as reaching the last island Laugh Tale. [[Douglas Bullet]] was an anime-exclusive former member of the Roger Pirates. The Roger Pirates disbanded prior to Roger's execution, with the current whereabouts of most of its members being unknown. ===Gol D. Roger=== {{nihongo|'''Gol D. Roger'''|ゴール・D・ロジャー|Gōru Dī Rojā}}, after gaining worldwide infamy as captain of the [[#Roger Pirates|Roger Pirates]], becomes better known as {{nihongo|'''Gold Roger'''|ゴールド・ロジャー|Gōrudo Rojā}}, the {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|King of the Pirates}}'''|海賊王|Kaizoku-Ō|{{lit}} "Pirate King"}}.{{gnr|ch|1|, |154|, |506}} Suffering from a terminal disease, he takes his crew on a complete voyage through the Grand Line before disbanding it and turning himself in to the [[World Government (One Piece)|World Government]], which claims to have captured him, while secretly entrusting his son, [[Portgas D. Ace|Ace]], to [[Monkey D. Garp]].{{gnr|ch|506}} At his execution, before [[Portgas D. Rouge|Rouge]] gives birth to Ace, and 22 years before the formation of the [[Straw Hats|Straw Hat Crew]], Roger inspires the "Great Pirate Era" by announcing that his treasure, the "One Piece", is up for the taking, though they will have to find it first.{{gnr|ch|1|, |506|, |550}} It is said after Roger's death that only [[Four Emperors (One Piece)#Edward Newgate|Whitebeard]] could match him in a fight and that he had the ability to hear "the voice of all things", which allowed him and his crew to learn the secret history of the world.{{gnr|ch|233|, |507}} He was also the original owner of Luffy's Straw Hat which fell into the possession of Shanks after his captain's death, with Shanks eventually passing it on to Luffy. Gol D. Roger has the highest known bounty in the series, with [[File:Berry (One Piece).svg|12px]]5,564,800,000.{{cite book|last=Oda|first=Eiichiro|title=Oden's Adventure|series=One Piece|volume=95|year=2019|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|isbn=978-1974718139|chapter=957 Ultimate}} Roger was a highly capable swordsman, skilled in advanced use of all three types of Haki.{{gnr|ch|966}} Roger is originally voiced by [[Chikao Ōtsuka]], and later by [[Masane Tsukayama]].{{cite video |title=One Piece Log Collection: East Blue |medium=DVD |language=ja |publisher=Avex Mode |year=2010}} A younger Roger is voiced by [[Takeshi Kusao]]. In the 4Kids adaptation, Roger is voiced by Frederick B. Owens.{{cite video |title=One Piece: Volume 1: King of the Pirates |medium=DVD |publisher=Viz Media |year=2006 |isbn=978-1-59861-000-0}} [[Eric Stuart]] initially voiced Roger before being replaced with Owens. In the Funimation English adaptation, he is voiced by Sean Hennigan.{{cite video |title=One Piece: Collection 1 |medium=DVD |publisher=Funimation Entertainment |year=2011 |isbn=978-1-4210-2341-0}} In the live-action series, he is portrayed by [[Michael Dorman]]. Roger is partially based on the real life pirate [[Olivier Levasseur]]. ===Silvers Rayleigh=== {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Silvers Rayleigh}}'''|シルバーズ・レイリー|Shirubāzu Reirī}} is a swordsman and the first mate of the Roger Pirates. Having encountered a young Roger in his youth, he joined the crew as his first mate, developing his swordsmanship to the point he is known as the {{nihongo|{{visible anchor|"'''Dark King'''"}}|冥王|Mei-Ō}} and considered to be Roger's right-hand man.{{Graphic novel reference|ch|603}} After Roger's death, Rayleigh retires on the [[Sabaody Archipelago]] as a ship coater and gambler.{{gnr|ch|500}} He encounters and reveals his identity to the Straw Hat Crew on their arrival, coating the ship and becoming a vital ally for the crew. Following the war between the [[Whitebeard Pirates]] and the [[World Government (One Piece)|World Government]], he trains [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]] to use Haki for two years.{{gnr|ch|503}}{{cite web |url=https://mein-mmo.de/en/the-5-most-loyal-allies-of-luffy-in-one-piece-who-are-not-crew-members,1242875/2/ |title=The 5 most loyal allies of Luffy in One Piece who are not crew members - Silvers Rayleigh |author=Esmeralda Eickemeyer |date=March 31, 2025 |website=mein-mmo.de}} He is one of the only men to be respected by the Kuja Tribe, having married their former empress [[World Government (One Piece)#Shakuyaku|Shakuyaku]]. Silvers Rayleigh is voiced by [[Keiichi Sonobe]] in the original Japanese version and by Bruce Carey in the Funimation dub. The character is named after the real life statesman and explorer [[Walter Raleigh]]. ===Scopper Gaban=== {{nihongo|'''Scopper Gaban'''|スコッパー・ギャバン|Sukoppā Gyaban}} was the navigator of the Roger Pirates. He is known for his proficient skill in wielding axes and amorous nature, later being nicknamed the "Left Hand of the Pirate King". During his time in the Roger Pirates, he was infamous for his constant one-night stands which he is ashamed of after being acquainted with Ripley. After Roger's death, he retired in Elbaph and fathered the half-giant Collun through the giant [[List of One Piece characters#Ripley|Ripley]].{{Graphic novel reference|ch|1139|,|1147}} During the fight against [[Imu (One Piece)|Imu]], Scopper Gaban loses his left arm. Scopper Gaban is voiced by [[Toshiyuki Morikawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Ian Sinclair (voice actor)|Ian Sinclair]] in the Funimation dub. === Crocus === {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Crocus}}'''|クロッカス|Kurokkasu}} was the doctor of the Roger Pirates, who joined late to help with Roger's. He is the sole human resident of the Twin Capes, and who takes care of the giant whale [[Laboon (One Piece)|Laboon]]. Crocus was voiced by [[Gorō Naya]] and [[Masuo Amada]] in the original Japanese version, and by Jerry Russell, Burl W. Proctor and Gregory Lush in the Funimation dub. In the live-action series, Crocus is portrayed by [[Clive Russell]].{{cite web |date=June 26, 2024 |title='One Piece' Adds Trio of Actors to Season 2 (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/one-piece-season-2-giant-warrior-pirates-crocus-1235932383/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}} ===Other Roger Pirates=== * {{nihongo|'''Donquino'''|ドンキーノ|Donkīno}}: A large man who is the helmsman of the Rogers Pirates. Moon Isaac Jr. is voiced by Yūsuke Shirooka in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Millet Pine'''|ミレ・パイン|Mire Pain}}: A short rotund man who is the interrogator/torturer of the Roger Pirates and wears a horned helmet. * {{nihongo|'''Rowing'''|ローウィング|Rowingu}}: A short rotund man who is the [[scholar]] of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Erio'''|エリオ}}: A slim man ina white fedora who is the [[Data broker|information broker]] of the Roger Pirates. Following the disbandment of the Rogers Pirates, Erio's whereabouts are unknown. Erio is voiced by Tom Henry in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Spencer'''|スペンサー|Supensā}}: The [[intelligence officer]] of the Roger Pirates. Spencer is voiced by Kristian Eros in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Petermoo'''|ピータームー|Pītāmū}}: A short man with an egg-shaped body who is the [[Gunner (rank)|gunner]] of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Blumarine'''|ブルマリン|Burumarin}}: A short older man who is the shipwright of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''MAX Marx'''|MAX マークス|Makkusu Mākusu}}: A tall muscular man who is the cook of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Seagull Guns Nozdon'''|シーガル・ガンズ・ノズドン|Shīgaru Ganzu Nozudon}}: A very tall and muscular man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. Seagull Guns Nozdon is voiced by Neiji Hirai in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Mr. Momora'''|Mr. モモラ|Misutā Momora}}: A very tall and thin man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. Mr. Momora is voiced by Ryōhei Arai in the original Japanese version and by Josh Putnam in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Jacksonbanner'''|ジャクソンバナー|Jakusonbanā}}: A tall slim man who is the musician of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Sunbell'''|サンベル|Sanberu}}: A fish-man of indeterminate species and a member of the Roger Pirates. Doringo is voiced by Yukinori Okuhata in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Ganryu'''|眼竜|Ganryū}}: A tall muscular man and a member of the Roger Pirates. Ganryu is voiced by Kazumasa Fukagawa in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''CB Gallant'''|CBギャラン|Shībī Gyaran}}: A large and very muscular man with short legs who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Yui'''|ユーイ|Yūi}}: A member of the Roger Pirates with wavy hair that goes straight up. * {{nihongo|'''Rangram'''|ラングラム|Ranguramu}}: A tall fit man who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Colonel Mugren'''|ミュグレン大佐|Myuguren Taisa}}: A large man with broad shoulders who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Bankuro'''|バンクロ}}: A short slender man with a puffy hair and beard who is a member of the Roger Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Yamon'''|ヤモン}}: A member of the Roger Pirates who fights with a spear. ==East Blue== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the East Blue sea. Former pirates in the East Blue include: * [[Zeff (One Piece)|"'''Red Foot'''" '''Zeff''']], now the Head Chef at Baratie. * '''[[Gaimon]]''' was a pirate until his body became trapped in a chest. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Koze}}'''|コゼ}} and {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Packy}}'''|パッキー|Pakkī}} were two members of the Yes Pirates. Koze is tall and thin while Packy is bulky and muscular. They were captured by [[Smoker (One Piece)|Smoker]] and [[Tashigi]] in Loguetown and arrested.{{gnr|ch|96}} * The [[#Usopp Pirates|Usopp Pirates]] (see below) * The [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]] were also stationed in this sea for several years until they were arrested. ===Black Cat Pirates=== The '''Black Cat Pirates''' are a cat-themed crew of pirates led by their captain [[#Kuro|Kuro]] who considers them as nothing but pawns to carry out his plans and, if he so pleases, to die for him.{{gnr|ch|38}} ====Kuro==== {{nihongo|'''Kuro'''|クロ|{{lit}} "Black"}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"Kuro of the Thousand Plans"|百計のクロ|Hyakkei no Kuro}}, is the captain of the [[#Black Cat Pirates|Black Cat Pirates]], who is known for his elaborate schemes.{{gnr|ch|26}} Wishing to leave his identity behind, and to escape the wearying pirate lifestyle of always being on the run,{{gnr|ch|37}} he uses the name '''Klahadore''' (クラハドール ''Kurahadōru'') and becomes butler to [[Kaya (One Piece)|Kaya]], a friend of [[Usopp]].{{gnr|ch|23}} He considers his crew as nothing but pawns to carry out his plans and, if he so pleases, to die for him.{{gnr|ch|38}} Kuro fights using a pair of gloves equipped with long, straight, single edged blades. Wearing these, he adopted his signature habit of adjusting his constantly slipping glasses by using only the palm of his hand to avoid cutting his face.{{gnr|ch|33}} In the anime, Kuro resumes pirate life following his defeat and sees that the bounty for Luffy has gone up following Arlong's defeat.{{cite episode |series=One Piece |series-link=One Piece (1999 TV series) |title=Bounty! Straw Hat Luffy Becomes Known to the World! |episode-link=One Piece season 1#ep45 |season=1 |number=45 |date=October 25, 2000 |network=[[Fuji Television]]}} In the Japanese anime television series, Kuro is voiced by [[Kōichi Hashimoto]]. In the 4Kids English adaptation, he is voiced by [[Gary Mack]] while his voice actor in the Funimation English adaptation is [[Kent Williams (voice actor)|Kent Williams]]. series)#ep4|The Pirates Are Coming]]|date=August 31, 2023}} ===Krieg Pirates=== The '''Krieg Pirates''' are a pirate crew led by [[#Don Krieg|Don Krieg]].{{gnr|ch|46}} The crew consisted of the largest pirate fleet in the East Blue until their ships were sunk by [[Dracule Mihawk]]. ====Don Krieg==== {{nihongo|'''Don {{visible anchor|Krieg}}'''|{{ruby-ja|首領|ドン}}・クリーク|Don Kurīku}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"Foul Play" Krieg|ダマシ討ちのクリーク|Damashi Uchi no Kurīku}}, is the captain of the [[#Krieg Pirates|Krieg Pirates]], a man well known for his underhanded tactics.{{gnr|ch|46}} Krieg does not care for his crew and bullies them into fearing and obeying him.{{gnr|ch|49}} He punishes those who fail him and those who show weakness.{{gnr|ch|61|f.}} Krieg wears a gilded suit of steel armor filled with hidden weapons such as guns, bombs, etc.{{gnr|ch|47}} Krieg also uses a weapon called the "Mighty Battle Spear", that is not only a spear, but can release explosions and remain intact. Don Krieg is voiced by [[Fumihiko Tachiki]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Marc Thompson (voice actor)|Marc Thompson]] and [[Andy Mullins (actor)|Andy Mullins]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. In the live-action series, Don Kireg is portrayed by Milton Schorr. Krieg is only a minor character in this version as opposed to the source material. His fleet is also not destroyed by Mihawk at the Baratie, rather at an unknown location and he does not survive his duel with Mihawk.{{cite episode|network=[[Netflix]]|series=One Piece|season=1|number=5|title=[[One Piece (2023 TV series)#ep5|Eat at Baratie!]]|date=August 31, 2023}}{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/one-piece-netflix-biggest-changes-from-anime/ |title=10 Biggest Changes Netflix's 'One Piece' Makes From the Anime |author=David Holman |date=October 17, 2023 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]}} ====Gin==== {{nihongo|'''Gin'''|ギン}} is Krieg's combat commander. He arrived at the Baratie restaurant hungry, being saved by Sanji, who offered him a plate of food, after which Gin was grateful to the cook. Because of this, he ended up rebelling against his captain, especially once he ended up being defeated by Luffy, because he lost all the respect he had for him, thinking that he was someone indestructible. Gin is voiced by [[Kenichi Ono]] in the original Japanese version. In the 4Kids dub, Gin is voiced by Peter Katana. In the Funimation dub, Gin is voiced by [[Illich Guardiola]] until 2014 and by [[David Matranga]] starting in the "Episode of East Blue" special. In the live-action series, Gin is portrayed by Litha Bam. ====Pearl==== {{nihongo|'''Pearl'''|パール|Pāru}} is a man protected by various shields. Although it is difficult to hurt him, he gets nervous if someone does the slightest injury to him, worrying everyone including his captain, as he begins to lose control. Pearl is voiced by Hiroyuki Kawamoto in the original Japanese version and by [[Dan Green (voice actor)|Dan Green]] and [[J. Michael Tatum]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. ===Usopp Pirates=== The '''{{visible anchor|Usopp Pirates}}''' were a pirate band formed in [[List of One Piece characters#Syrup Village|Syrup Village]] by Captain [[Usopp]] and three younger children: {{nihongo|'''Carrot'''|にんじん|Ninjin}}, {{nihongo|'''Pepper'''|ピーマン|Pīman}}, and {{nihongo|'''Onion'''|たまねぎ|Tamanegi}}. The Straw Hats and Usopp Pirates fought against the Black Cat Pirates to defend their village. Usopp tearfully disbanded the Usopp Pirates afterwards to set sail with the Straw Hats.{{gnr|ch|40}}{{gnr|ch|41}} Carrot is voiced by Noriko Yoshitake in the original Japanese version and by Jim Napolitano and Kate Oxley in the 4Kids and Funimation dubs respectively. Pepper is voiced by [[Haruhi Terada]] in the earlier parts of the original Japanese version and by Miyuki Kawasho starting in Episode 291 and by Kevin Kolack and [[Cherami Leigh]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dubs (except for the English dub of the video game ''One Piece: Unlimited Adventure'', where she is voiced by [[Laura Bailey]]). Onion is voiced by [[Makiko Ohmoto]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Oliver Wyman (actor)|Oliver Wyman]] and [[Cynthia Cranz]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dubs respectively. Usopp is the only member of the Usopp Pirates who appears in the live-action series. ==North Blue== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the North Blue sea. ===Bellamy Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Bellamy Pirates'''|ベラミー海賊団|Beramī Kaizokudan}} was a pirate crew originating from the North Blue and allies with the [[Donquixote Pirates]]. ====Bellamy==== {{nihongo|{{vanchor|'''Bellamy''' "'''the Hyena'''"|Bellamy the Hyena}}|ハイエナのベラミー|Haiena no Beramī}} was the captain of the Bellamy Pirates, a blonde-haired man with the power of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Boing-Boing Fruit|バネバネの実|Bane Bane no Mi}}, which allows him to turn his legs into springs to bounce off surfaces and gain momentum for his attacks.{{gnr|ch|230|f.}} After his defeat at the hands of [[Monkey D. Luffy|Luffy]], [[Donquixote Doflamingo]] dismisses Bellamy, who later becomes a fighter in Dressrosa.{{gnr|ch|706}} Bellamy and Luffy befriended each other in Dressrosa and after Luffy defeated Doflamingo, Bellamy was present during the formation of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet.{{gnr|ch|799}} In the anime television series, Bellamy's voice actor is [[Wataru Takagi]]. In the 4Kids English adaptation, he is voiced by [[Andrew Rannells]]. In the Funimation English adaptation, his voice is supplied by [[Justin Cook]]. The character is named after the real life pirate [[Samuel Bellamy]]. ====Other Bellamy Pirates members==== The rest of the Bellamy Pirates consisted of: * "'''Big Knife'''" {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Sarquiss|Sarkies}}'''|サーキース|Sākīsu|alt. "Sarkies"}}: A blue-haired bespectacled man who is Bellamy's first mate.{{gnr|ch|223}} He is voiced by [[Yuji Ueda]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Duncan Brannan]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Lily'''|リリー|Rirī}}: A woman who often accompanied Sarquiss.{{gnr|ch|223}} She is voiced by Yuko Sumitomo in the original Japanese version and by [[Trina Nishimura]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Eddy'''|エディ|Edi}}: The Bellamy Pirates' navigator. He is voiced by [[Hiroshi Kamiya]] in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, he is voiced by Andy Baldwin in episodes 149 and 150 and by [[Zach Bolton]] in Episode 207. * {{nihongo|'''Mjure'''|ミュレ|Myure}}: The Bellamy Pirates' doctor. She is voiced by Yuko Shioyama in the original Japanese version and by [[Colleen Clinkenbeard]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Hewitt'''|ヒューイット|Hyūitto}}: The Bellamy Pirates' cook. * {{nihongo|'''Rivers'''|リヴァーズ|Rivāzu}}: The Bellamy Pirates' sniper. He is voiced by [[Masaya Takatsuka]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Patrick Seitz]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Ross'''|ロス|Rosu}}: The Bellamy Pirates' swordsman. He is voiced by Osamu Ryutani in the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, he is voiced by Scott Cantrell in earlier appearances and by Tyson Rinehart starting in Episode 207. * {{nihongo|'''Mani'''|マニ}}: The Bellamy Pirates' combatant. She is voiced by Brigette Goudeau in the Funimation dub. ===Caribou Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Caribou Pirates'''|カリブー海賊団|Karibū kaizoku-dan}} is a pirate group that encountered the Straw Hat Crew after they got back together. *{{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Caribou}}'''|カリブー|Karibū}}: Nicknamed "'''Wet-Haired'''" , is a rookie pirate and co-captain of the Caribou Pirates along with his young brother Coribou. He consumed the Swamp-Swamp Fruit which enables him to generate, control, and become a "[[swamp]]".{{cite web |url=https://www.soapcentral.com/anime/everything-know-caribou-one-piece |title=Everything we know about Caribou in One Piece |author=Akihito Chakma |date=July 29, 2025 |website=soapcentral.com}} Caribou is voiced by [[Masaki Terasoma]] in the original Japanese version and by Andrew Kasten in the Funimation dub. *{{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Coribou}}'''|コリブー|Koribū}}: Nicknamed "'''Blood Splatterer'''", is the egg-shaped younger brother of Caribou and co-captain of the Caribou Pirates. He wears a lizard on his head as a hairstyle. Coribou is voiced by Kohei Fukuhara in the original Japanese version and by Dalton Tindall in the Funimation dub. *{{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Momoo}}'''|モーム|Mōmu}}: A giant sea cow from the Grand Line (a Sea Beast with the head of a cow). He was originally introduced as part of the [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]], being utilized by them as a method of intimidation towards the residents of the Conomi Islands. After Arlong Pirates' defeat, he was captured and employed as a draft animal by the Caribou Pirates. ==West Blue== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the West Blue sea. ===Rumbar Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Rumbar Pirates'''|ルンバー海賊団|Runbā Kaizokudan}} were a musical band of pirates active in the West Blue before the rise of Gol D. Roger. Their captain, Yorki, and other crew members left after contracting an incurable disease and the others were fatally poisoned by enemy pirates. [[Brook (One Piece)|Brook]] served as the second captain of the crew before his death, but was the sole survivor due to eating the Revive-Revive Fruit. ====Yorki==== {{nihongo|'''Yorki'''|ヨーキ|Yōki}}, also known as {{nihongo|"'''Calico'''" '''Yorki'''|キャラコのヨーキ|Kyarako no Yōki}}, was the captain of the Rumbar Pirates prior to his resignation after contracting a mysterious illness.{{gnr|ch|487}} Under Yorki, they entered the Grand Line at Reverse Mountain with the baby island whale [[Laboon (One Piece)|Laboon]].{{gnr|ch|487}} After Yorki left, [[Brook (One Piece)|Brook]] served as the acting captain, and the group were completely wiped out by an unknown foe approximately 50 years before the events aboard Thriller Bark with their doctor being killed by an enemy pirate crew that specialized in poison-tainted weapons.{{gnr|ch|488}} In the original Japanese version of the anime, Yorki is voiced by Yasunori Masutani in the Episode 63 and by Eiji Takemoto in later appearances, while in the Funimation dub he is voiced by Charles Baker in the Episode 63 and by Chris Hury in later appearances. In the live-action series, he is portrayed by Richard Gau.{{cite web |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/one-piece-season-2-laboon-whale-explained |title=Inside Laboon's Heartbreaking Saga in ''ONE PIECE'' Season 2 |author=Keisha Hatchett |date=March 16, 2026 |website=Netflix Tudum}} His epithet is based on that of the real life pirate [[Calico Jack]]. ==South Blue== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the South Blue sea. ===Foxy Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Foxy Pirates'''|フォクシー海賊団|Fokushī Kaizokudan}} is a crew specializing in a pirate game known as the "Davy Back Fight" wherein pirate crews can win crewmen from their opponents and their Jolly Roger. One example is when he won the Fanged Toad Pirates' captain Kibagaeru, its unnamed helmsman, and its unnamed navigator as well as their Jolly Roger leaving the rest of the Fanged Toad Pirates in disarray.{{gnr|ch|306}} The crew is led by [[#Foxy|Foxy]].{{gnr|ch|309}} ====Foxy==== {{nihongo|'''Foxy'''|フォクシー|Fokushī}}, nicknamed {{nihongo|"'''Silver Fox'''"|銀ギツネ|Gin Gitsune}}, is the cheater and trickster captain of the [[#Foxy Pirates|Foxy Pirates]].{{gnr|ch|307}} Though he acts supremely confident most of the time, he is extremely sensitive to insults or criticism.{{gnr|ch|306}} Having eaten the {{nihongo|Slow-Slow Fruit|ノロノロの実|Noro Noro no Mi}}, Foxy can emit a beam with microscopic particles from his hands which can temporarily slow down any object, reducing its [[velocity]] while preserving [[kinetic energy]].{{gnr|ch|309}} Although in the manga where Foxy only appears as the main antagonist of a story arc, he is a recurring opponent of Luffy's crew in the anime. Foxy is voiced by [[Bin Shimada]] in the original Japanese version and by Jonathan Brooks in the Funimation English dub. ====Other Foxy Pirates members==== Other members of Foxy's crew include: * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Porche}}'''|ポルチェ|Poruche}}: The crew's [[Japanese idol|idol]]. Porche is voiced by [[Sara Nakayama]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Tia Ballard]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Hamburg}}'''|ハンバーグ|Hanbāgu}}: A gorilla-like human who occasionally serves as Foxy's mount and leader of the Groggy Monsters.{{gnr|ch|305}} Hamburg is voiced by [[Hirohiko Kakegawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Scott Freeman (voice actor)|Scott Freeman]] in the Funimation dub. Former members of Foxy's crew include: * {{nihongo|'''Pickles'''|ピクルス|Pikurusu}}: A large and husky man who is a member of the Groggy Monsters. Pickles is voiced by Osamu Ryūtani in the original Japanese version and by Bradford Jackson in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Big Pan'''|ビッグパン|Biggu Pan}}: A Wotan which is a result of a union between a giant and a fish-man, with his fish-type being a [[pond loach]]. He is a member of the Groggy Monsters. Big Pan is voiced by [[Mahito Ōba]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Andrew Chandler (actor)|Andrew Chandler]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Kibagaeru'''|キバガエル}}: The former captain of the Fanged Toad Pirates who Foxy claimed in the Davy Back Fight against them, leaving his crew in disarray and dying in a storm. In the [[One Piece (1999 TV series)|anime-exclusive]] "Foxy Returns Arc", Kibagaeru briefly took over the Foxy Pirates. After being defeated by the Straw Hat Crew, Kibagaeru allowed Foxy to lead the Foxy Pirates again. Kibagaeru is voiced by [[Takashi Nagasako]] in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Itomimizu'''|イトミミズ}}: The announcer and commentator. Itomimizu is voiced by [[Keiichi Nanba]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Ian Sinclair (voice actor)|Ian Sinclair]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Chuchun'''|チュチューン|Chuchūn}}: Itomimizu's pet giant sparrow and transport. Chuchun's vocal effects are provided by [[Hiroaki Hirata]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Chris Cason]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Capote'''|カポーティ|Kapōti}}: A [[billfish]]-type fish-man. Capote is voiced by [[Hiroshi Tsuchida]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Phil Parsons (voice actor)|Phil Parsons]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Monda'''|モンダ}}: A star shark. Monda's vocal effects are provided by [[Masaya Takatsuka]] in the original Japanese version and by [[John Burgmeier]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Gina'''|ジーナ|Jīna}}: A shipwright for the Foxy Pirates. * {{nihongo|'''Sonieh'''|ソニエ|Sonie}}: The leader of the Foxy Pirates' 50 mechanics. * {{nihongo|'''Donovan'''|ドノバン|Donoban}}: One of the Foxy Pirates' 50 mechanics. * '''[[Tony Tony Chopper]]''' also temporarily became a member during the Davy Back Fight. The Foxy Pirates also have several [[One Piece (1999 TV series)|anime]]-exclusive members: * '''Mashikaku''': A large and rectangular man. Mashikaku is voiced by [[Mike McFarland]] in the Funimation dub. * '''Chiqicheetah''': A crew member whose unnamed Devil Fruit enables him to turn into a [[cheetah]] and a cheetah-human hybrid. Chiqicheetah is voiced by [[Hiroshi Tsuchida]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Jessie James Grelle]] in the Funimation dub. * '''Jube''': A [[squid]]-type fish-man. Jube is voiced by [[Hirohiko Kakegawa]] in the original Japanese version and by Charles Baker in the Funimation dub. * '''Girarin''': An unspecified fish-man. Girarin is voiced by [[Masaya Takatsuka]] in the original Japanese version and by Z. Charles Bolton in the Funimation dub. * '''Rokuroshi''': The head referee for Hit and Dead Ball. Rokurokushi is voiced by Tomohisa Asō in the original Japanese version and by [[Tony Oliver]] in the Funimation dub. * '''[[Nico Robin]]''' also temporarily became a member during the Davy Back Fight in anime-exclusive events. ==Paradise, Grand Line== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from Paradise, the first half of the Grand Line sea. ===Bliking Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Bliking Pirates'''|ブリキング海賊団|Burikingu Kaizokudan}} are a group of pirates from Drum Island. Some of its members later join the [[List of One Piece characters#Evil Black Drum Kingdom|Evil Black Drum Kingdom]]. * '''[[Wapol]]''': The former captain of the crew. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Chess}}'''|チェス|Chesu}}: An underling of Wapol who is a skilled archer. Jones]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. They were defeated by Tony Tony Chopper. In ''One Piece: Stampede'', Chess and Kuromarimo split back into their original bodies. Kuromarimo is voiced by [[Kenji Nomura]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Jamie McGonnigal]] and [[Charles Baker (actor)|Charles Baker]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. In the live-action series he is renamed as "K.M.", and is portrayed by [[Anton David Jeftha]]. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Robson}}'''|ロブソン|Robuson}}: A White Walkie (a creature resembling woolly hippopotamus), which serves as a mount for Wapol. Robson's vocal effects are provided by [[Kenji Nomura]] in the original Japanese version and by Kyle Phillips in the Funimation dub. The [[Episode of Chopper Plus: Bloom in the Winter, Miracle Sakura|9th movie]] also includes Wapol's brother [[Musshuru]] as part of the crew. ===Brownbeard Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Brownbeard Pirates'''|茶ひげ海賊団|Cha hi-ge kaizoku-dan}} are a pirate group who had their lower body parts replaced by animal parts by [[#Trafalgar Law|Trafalgar Law]] after they were badly defeated by [[#Basil Hawkins|Basil Hawkins]]. ====Brownbeard==== {{nihongo|'''Chadros Higelyges'''|チャドロス・ヒゲリゲス|Chadorosu Higerigesu}}, better known as {{nihongo|'''Brownbeard'''|茶ひげ|Chahige}}, is a large man and the captain of the Brownbeard Pirates who has large [[alligator]] legs added by Law, giving him a [[centaur]]-like appearance. He and his remaining crew members helped to form the Centaur Patrol Unit which worked for Caesar Clown. After Caesar Clown was defeated, Brownbeard and his crew surrendered to Smoker. Brownbeard is voiced by Yasuhiko Tokuyama in Episode 491 of the original Japanese version, [[Kazunari Tanaka]] in Episode 511 of the original Japanese version, and [[Masashi Sugawara]] starting in Episode 583 of the original Japanese version. In the Funimation dub, he is voiced by Randy E. Aguebor. ====Other Brownbeard Pirates members==== * {{nihongo|'''Smooge'''|スムージ|Sumūji}}: A member of the Brownbeard Pirates who resembles a normal centaur. Chappe is voiced by [[Eiji Takemoto]] in the original Japanese version and by Chris Thurman in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Run'''|ルン}}: A member of the Brownbeard Pirates who resembles a [[drider]]. Run is voiced by [[Masaya Takatsuka]] in the original Japanese version and by Timothy McNamee in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Hyoutauros'''|ヒョウタウロス|Hyōtaurosu}}: A jaguar-like centaur and member of the Brownbeard Pirates. Hyoutauros is voiced by Kōhei Fukuhara in the original Japanese version and by Ray Gestaut in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''Kirintauros'''|キリンタウロス|Kirintaurosu}}: A giraffe-like centaur and member of the Brownbeard Pirates. Kirintauros is voiced by [[Yūsei Oda]] in the original Japanese version and by Phillip Annarella in the Funimation dub. * Unidentified members include a deer-type centaur, a rhinoceros-type centaur, a zebra-type centaur, and a [[tapir]]-type centaur. ==={{visible anchor|Monkey Mountain Allied Force|Saruyama Alliance}}=== The {{nihongo|'''Monkey Mountain Allied Force'''|猿山連合軍|Saruyama Rengō-gun}} is a group formed between three pirate captains. Originally stationed in Jaya, they helped the Straw Hat Crew in getting to [[Skypiea]]. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Mont Blanc Cricket}}|モンブラン・クリケット|Monburan Kuriketto}}''': The leader of the Monkey Mountain Allied Forces who is a descendant of [[Mont Blanc Noland]], who was known as "Liar Noland" because of lying about the existence of a City of Gold. Osborne. ==Sea Floor== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from the sea floor, specifically from the [[Fish-Man Island]]. ===Arlong Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Arlong Pirates'''|アーロン一味|Āron Ichimi}} are a pirate crew consisting mostly of [[List of aquatic humanoids|fishmen]] led by the [[sawshark]]-type fish-man [[#Arlong|Arlong]] and several officers. [[#Hatchan|Hatchan]], [[#Momoo|Momoo]] and [[Nami (One Piece)|Nami]] used to be members until the latter left the crew following its defeat by the [[Straw Hats]].{{gnr|ch|69|, |75|, |93|f.}} ====Arlong==== {{nihongo|"'''Saw-Tooth'''" '''Arlong'''|ノコギリのアーロン|Nokogiri no Āron}} is a [[sawshark]]-type fish-man and fish-man supremacist.{{gnr|ch|69|, |71}} Growing up in a rough part of [[Fish-Man Island]], he becomes captain of the Arlong Pirates, who temporarily merge with other fishmen to form the [[#Sun Pirates|Sun Pirates]].{{gnr|ch|621|, |624}} Arlong's powerful jaws have rapidly re-growing teeth capable of rending stone.{{gnr|ch|90}} His favorite weapon is the sword-like {{nihongo|Shark Saw|キリバチ|Kiribachi}} with its six tooth-shaped blades.{{gnr|ch|92}} In the original Japanese series, Arlong's voice actor is [[Jūrōta Kosugi]].{{cite video |year=2010 |title=One Piece Log Collection: Nami |medium=DVD |publisher=Avex Mode |language=ja}} In the 4Kids English adaptation, he is voiced by [[David Wills (voice actor)|David Wills]].{{cite video |year=2007 |title=One Piece: Volume 7: New Crew |medium=DVD |publisher=Viz Media |isbn=978-1-59861-006-2 }} In the Funimation English adaptation, his voice is supplied by [[Chris Rager]].{{cite video |year=2011 |title=One Piece: Collection 2 |medium=DVD |publisher=Funimation Entertainment |isbn=978-1-4210-2404-2 }} ====Hatchan==== {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Hatchan|Hachi}}'''|はっちゃん}}, often called {{nihongo|'''Hachi'''|ハチ}}, is an octopus-type fish-man first introduced as an officer of the [[#Arlong Pirates|Arlong Pirates]].{{gnr|ch|73}} Being half octopus, he can spit large quantities of black ink and use suction pads to stick to walls.{{gnr|ch|83|f.}} He fights using six swords, holding one in each arm-tentacle.{{gnr|ch|84}} After his crew is defeated by the [[Straw Hats|Straw Hat Crew]], he escapes from captivity and opens a floating [[takoyaki]] restaurant.{{gnr|ch|182|–|228|: chapter cover pages}} Hatchan becomes close friends with [[Camie (One Piece)|Camie]] and [[List of One Piece characters#Pappagu|Pappagu]].{{gnr|ch|490|f.}} He later befriends the Straw Hats when they visit the Sabaody Archipelago.{{gnr|ch|496|, |506}} Hatchan's voice actor is [[Toshiyuki Morikawa]]. In the 4Kids and Funimation English adaptations, his voice is supplied by [[Sean Schemmel]] and [[George Manley]], respectively. In the live-action series, Hatchan was replaced by a [[barred knifejaw]]–type fish man (portrayed by Jaid Norman), who was unnamed in the manga and in this series was named "Hachi" after him. Hatchan's absence was due to budget constraints that prevented season one from having ten episodes, though showrunner Matt Owens plans to have him appear in said adaption during the Sabaody Archipelago arc.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH98uw5NY_8|title=Hasan Interviews One Piece Showrunner, Matt Owens|quote=[1:31:13]|publisher=Hasanabi Productions|website=[[YouTube]]|date=2024-03-24|access-date=2025-07-14}} ====Kuroobi==== {{nihongo|'''Kuroobi'''|クロオビ|Kurōbi}} is a [[manta ray]]–type fish-man who uses "Fishman Karate", and one of the officers of the Arlong Pirates. He confronts [[Sanji (One Piece)|Sanji]] at Arlong Park, ending up being defeated. Kuroobi is voiced by [[Hisao Egawa]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Sean Schemmel]] and [[Patrick Seitz]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. In the live-action series, he is portrayed by Jandre le Roux.{{cite web |last1=Aberl |first1=Joseph |title='Tomb Raider' Actor to Play Kuroobi in Netflix's 'One Piece' |url=https://www.murphysmultiverse.com/tomb-raider-actor-to-play-kuroobi-in-netflixs-one-piece/ |website=Murphy's Multiverse |access-date=March 8, 2023 |date=March 8, 2023 |archive-date=March 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308232839/https://www.murphysmultiverse.com/tomb-raider-actor-to-play-kuroobi-in-netflixs-one-piece/ |url-status=live}} ====Choo==== {{nihongo|'''Choo'''|チュウ|Chū}} is a [[Japanese whiting]]–type fish-man who spits water as if they were firing bullets and one of the officers of the Arlong Pirates. He confronts [[Usopp]], ending up being defeated. Choo is voiced by [[Masaya Onosaka]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Tom Wayland]] and [[Jay Hickman (actor)|Jay Hickman]] in the 4Kids and Funimation dub respectively. In the live-action series, he is portrayed by Len-Barry Simons. ===Fisher Tiger=== {{nihongo|'''Fisher Tiger'''|フィッシャー・タイガー|Fisshā Taigā}} is a [[Sparidae|sea bream]]-type fish-man who was the founder and first captain of the [[#Sun Pirates|Sun Pirates]]. Fisher Tiger, Arlong and Jimbei grew up together as sworn brothers from the Fish-Man District.{{gnr|ch|621}} Fisher Tiger was later enslaved before being freed by [[Shanks (One Piece)|Shanks]] at Mary Geoise. Fisher Tiger went on to escape and free other enslaved peoples, including mermen, fish-men, and [[#Boa Hancock|Boa Hancock]] and her two sisters. After he escaped, Fisher Tiger, Jimbei, the Arlong Pirates, the Macro Pirates, and the newly freed Fish-men and mermen adopted the Sun insignia as founding members of the Sun Pirates. After he died from blood loss following an ambush by the Marines, he was succeeded by Jimbei. Fisher Tiger is voiced by [[Kōji Ishii]] in the original Japanese version and by Gabe Kunda in the Funimation dub. ===Macro Pirates=== The {{nihongo|'''Macro Pirates'''|マクロ一味|Makuro Ichimi}} are a crew formed by former members of the [[#Sun Pirates|Sun Pirates]] who now work as kidnappers. They kidnapped [[Camie (One Piece)|Camie]] multiple times. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Macro}}'''|マクロ|Makuro}}: A [[pelican eel]]-type fish-man and captain of the crew.{{gnr|ch|492}} Macro is voiced by [[Takashi Nagasaki]] in the original Japanese version and by Hunter Scott in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Gyaro}}'''|ギャロ}}: A [[Telescope (goldfish)|pop-eyed goldfish]]-type fish-man.{{gnr|ch|492}} Gyaro is voiced by [[Yūsei Oda]] in the original Japanese version and by Patric Carroll in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Tansui}}'''|タンスイ}}: An [[arowana]]-type fish-man.{{gnr|ch|492}} ===New Fish-Man–Flying Pirates Alliance=== The {{nihongo|'''New Fish-Man Pirates'''|新魚人海賊団|Shin-Gyojin Kaizoku-dan}} are a pirate group of fish-men [[supremacist]]s who ally with the {{nihongo|'''Flying Pirates'''|フライング海賊団|Furaingu Kaizokudan}}, a group of fish-man pirates founded by Vander Decken IX. Together they plot the complete destruction of Fish-Man Island by initiating a [[coup d'etat]]. Jones broadcasts a message to the island, announcing that he will execute Neptune, its current ruler, to [[Dictatorship|take over the kingdom]], and then kill the Straw Hat Crew. However, Luffy eventually teams up with [[Jimbei]] to launch a combined assault on the pirate crews, defeating them and saving Fish-Man Island. ====New Fish-Man Pirates==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Hordy Jones|Hody|Hordy|Hody Jones}}'''|ホーディ・ジョーンズ|Hōdi Jōnzu}}: A [[great white shark]]-type fish-man and the leader of the New Fishman Pirates.{{gnr|ch|631}} Hordy is responsible for assassinating Otohime, the queen of [[Fish-Man Island]]. He uses a Sea Giraffe as his steed. Hordy Jones is voiced by [[Jōji Nakata]] in the original Japanese version and by [[Larry Brantley]] in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Dosun}}'''|ドスン}}: A [[hammerhead shark]]-type fish-man who uses a Sea Elephant as his steed. Dosun is voiced by [[Takahiro Yoshimizu]] in the original Japanese version and by Christian Taylor in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Zeo}}'''|ゼオ}}: A [[Japanese wobbegong]]-type fish-man who uses a Sea Rhinoceros as his steed. Zeo is voiced by [[Shintarō Asanuma]] in the original Japanese version and by Nazeeh Tarsha in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Daruma}}'''|ダルマ}}: A [[cookiecutter shark]]-type fish-man. Daruma is voiced by [[Hisayoshi Suganuma]] in the original Japanese version and by Oscar Seung in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Ikaros Munch}}'''|イカロス・ムッヒ|Ikarosu Muhhi}}: A [[giant squid]]-type fish-man. Ikaros Munch is voiced by Keiji Hirai in the original Japanese version and by Ethan Gallardo in the Funimation dub. * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Hyouzou}}'''|ヒョウゾウ|Hyōzō}}: A poisonous [[blue-ringed octopus]]-type merman who serves as the New Fishman Pirates' assassin and uses a Sea Gorilla as his steed. Hyouzou is voiced by Tetsuo Sakaguchi in the original Japanese version and by Dave Woodard in the Funimation dub. ====Flying Pirates==== * {{nihongo|'''{{vanchor|Vander Decken IX}}'''|バンダー・デッケン九世|Bandā Dekken Kyūsei}}: A [[Japanese bullhead shark]]-type fish-man and the leader of the Flying Pirates. He possesses the power of the Paramecia-type {{nihongo|Target-Target Fruit|マトマトの実|Mato-Mato no Mi}} that enables him to lock on any target at will so long as he touches the target first. Despite lacking the ability to swim, he retains the ability to survive underwater. Vander Decken IX is voiced by [[Wataru Takagi]] in the original Japanese version and by Jim Foronda in the Funimation dub. * '''[[#Wadatsumi|Wadatsumi]]''' is a former member of the crew. ==New World, Grand Line== The following are pirates and pirate crews originating from New World, the second half of the Grand Line sea. ===Giant Warrior Pirates=== The '''Giant Warrior Pirates''' are a group of pirates originating from [[Elbaph]]. After a brief disbandment, they reunite to help Luffy fight the Marines on Egghead. ====Brogy and Dorry==== {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Brogy}}'''|ブロギー|Burogī}} and {{nihongo|'''{{visible anchor|Dorry}}'''|ドリー|Dorī}}, co-captains of the Giant Warrior Pirates, are two giants living on Little Garden, where they have dueled for over a century. The [[Straw Hats]] saved them from being caught by the members of [[Baroque Works]] led by [[Galdino (One Piece)|Mr. 3]]. After ending their duel after the time skip, Brogy and Dorry head to Elbaph, they to help Shanks to fight the Kid Pirates. Shortly afterwards they traveled to Egghead, where they met up with the Straw Hats again, and guided them to Elbaph. Brogy is voiced by [[Tetsu Inada]] in the original Japanese version and by Jonathan C. Osborne in the Funimation dub. Dorry is voiced by [[Daisuke Gōri]] in the original Japanese version and by Bob Carter in the Funimation dub. In the live-action series, Brogy and Dorry are portrayed by Brendan Murray and [[Werner Coetser]], respectively.{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/one-piece-season-2-giant-warrior-pirates-crocus-1235932383/ |title='One Piece' Adds Trio of Actors to Season 2 (Exclusive) |date=June 26, 2024 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}} ====Oimo==== {{nihongo|'''Oimo'''|オイモ}} is a 52 ft. giant and member of the Giant Warrior Pirates. After their disbandment, Oimo worked as a guard at Enies Lobby. He later defects from the World Government. By the time the Straw Hat Crew were on Egghead, Oimo has rejoined the Giant Warrior Pirates and arrived on Egghead to help them. Oimo is revealed to have a grandson named Olav. Oimo is voiced by Hiroshi Okamoto in the original Japanese version and by Tyson Rhinehart in the Funimation dub. ====Kashii==== {{nihongo|'''Kashii'''|カーシー|Kāshī}} is a 55 ft. giant and member of the Giant Warrior Pirates. After their disbandment, Kashii worked as a guard at Enies Lobby. He later defects from the World Government. By the time the Straw Hat Crew were on Egghead, Kashii has rejoined the Giant Warrior Pirates and arrived on Egghead to help them. Kashii is voiced by Kōhei Fukuhara in the original Japanese version and by Jeff Johnson in the Funimation dub. ====Other Giant Warrior Pirates==== * {{nihongo|'''Bjorn'''|ビョルン|Byorun}}: A giant and member of the Giant Warrior Pirates. Bjorn is voiced by [[Fukushi Ochiai]] in the original Japanese version. * {{nihongo|'''Sig'''|シグ|Shigu}}: A goggles-wearing giant and member of the Giant Warrior Pirates.
